15.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
15.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

16.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

16.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

17.meaning: 'He/it calls, summons, invites, calls upon, prays to' — a verb for calling out to someone, inviting them, or supplicating.
17.grammar: An imperfect (present/ongoing) verb from a weak-final root, third-person masculine singular ('he/it'). The ya- prefix marks the masculine singular subject; the stem ends in a long ū from the weak final letter.

18.meaning: 'To Him' or 'toward Him' — the preposition expressing direction or endpoint ('to / toward') combined with a pronoun referring to a single masculine person, indicating motion or attention directed at him.
18.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The base 'ilā shifts to 'ilay- when a pronoun is added. The suffix -hi is the third-person masculine singular object of a preposition, 'him'; its -i vowel is the form the pronoun takes after the 'ay' sound.

19.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
19.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

20.meaning: An adverb of time meaning 'before / beforehand / previously,' pointing to a moment or state that precedes something else in time. When used with the final vowel -u (qablu), it stands cut off from an explicit following noun, conveying 'before(hand)' or 'previously' in an absolute sense — the thing it is 'before' is understood rather than stated.
20.grammar: An adverb of time. The final -u ending here is the indeclinable (mabnī) form taken when the word is severed from a following genitive: rather than 'before X,' it means 'before(hand)' on its own, with the reference point left implicit.
20.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to come before, precede, be in front; to receive/accept

21.meaning: 'And he made / appointed / rendered' — the connector 'and' joined to a past-tense verb meaning to make something into something, to fashion or appoint it. It can mean to create, to assign, or to cause a thing to become a certain way.
21.grammar: The connective wa- ('and') prefixed to a past-tense (perfect) verb. The bare verb with its final -a vowel denotes a completed act by a third-person masculine singular subject ('he made/did').
21.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, render, appoint, place

22.meaning: A two-part word: the preposition 'li-' meaning 'to', 'for', or 'belonging to', attached to the name 'Allah'. It conveys 'to Allah' or 'for Allah'.
22.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('to/for') pulls the following noun into the genitive case, which is why 'Allah' ends in '-i' (llāhi). The '-i' ending is the regular result of a noun governed by a preposition.

23.meaning: The plural of 'nidd': 'rivals', 'equals', or 'peers' — things set up as comparable or equal to something else, especially false objects of worship set up alongside Allah.
23.grammar: 'andād' is a broken (irregular) plural of 'nidd'. The '-an' ending (tanwīn al-fatḥ) marks an indefinite noun in the accusative case, the case typically used for the direct object of a verb ('… some rivals').
23.root: ن-د-د (n-d-d) — to be equal/rival, a counterpart or match

24.meaning: So as to lead astray; in order that he/it mislead or cause to wander from the right path. It expresses the purpose or result of leading someone into error.
24.grammar: The particle 'li-' ('so that / in order to') governs the verb, which is why it ends in '-a' (the subjunctive, used for purpose). The 'yu-' prefix marks a third-person 'he/it' subject in a causative form (Form IV: 'to make go astray').
24.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to go astray, lose the way, err

25.meaning: A preposition meaning 'on behalf of,' 'for,' 'about,' or 'away from.' It often conveys removing a burden from someone or acting in their place.

parts.en: on behalf of / for / away from

25.grammar: A preposition (a linking particle). It governs the noun that follows it, putting that noun into the genitive case. It does not change form.

26.meaning: "His way / His path" — the noun for a road, path, or way, here carrying the attached pronoun "His" (referring to Allah); idiomatically, the path or cause of Allah.
26.grammar: A masculine noun with the attached possessive pronoun "-hi" ("his/His"). The pronoun appears in its "-hi" form (with the "i" vowel), which is used when the noun is in the genitive — i.e., after a preposition or when linked in an "of"-type relation to a preceding word.

27.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
27.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

28.meaning: Enjoy / take benefit — tamattaʿ is a command form meaning 'enjoy yourself', 'take your pleasure', often used in a dismissive or threatening sense.
28.grammar: Form V imperative (second masculine singular) from root m-t-ʿ, meaning to enjoy or to derive pleasure. The Form V pattern tafaʿʿala adds a reflexive nuance. In context it is a rhetorical command expressing contempt — 'go ahead and enjoy your disbelief, for a short while'.
28.root: م-ت-ع (m-t-ʿ) — to enjoy, to benefit from, to have use of

29.meaning: In your disbelief — bi- is the preposition 'in/with'; kuf'rika is 'your disbelief/ingratitude', with the possessive suffix -ka 'your'.

parts.en: your (second person singular masculine possessive suffix)

29.grammar: Bi- is a preposition of accompaniment/state. Kufr is a noun from root k-f-r in the genitive after bi-. The suffix -ka is the second-person masculine singular possessive. Context: you are told to enjoy yourself in your state of disbelief — a warning that this enjoyment will be brief.
29.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to disbelieve, to be ungrateful, to cover (the truth)

30.meaning: A small amount; little, few, slight. It describes something modest in quantity, degree, or duration.
30.grammar: An adjective/noun in the indefinite accusative case, shown by the -an ending (tanwīn fatḥa). This ending commonly marks a direct object, or functions adverbially to mean 'a little' / 'slightly' / 'for a short while'.
30.root: ق-ل-ل (q-l-l) — to be little, few, scant

31.meaning: 'Indeed you' — an emphasis particle meaning 'truly / indeed' joined to the pronoun 'you', used to open a statement with certainty and stress about the person addressed.
31.grammar: The emphasis particle 'inna' ('indeed, truly') with an attached pronoun. 'inna' adds strong assertion to a sentence and grammatically governs the following noun/pronoun in the accusative. The suffix '-ka' means 'you' (masculine singular) as its subject.

32.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
32.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

33.meaning: Companions, associates, fellows; those who keep company with or belong to a thing — people closely bound to something (often 'people/inhabitants of …').
33.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural of ṣāḥib ('companion'). The final -i is the genitive ending, which typically links the word to a following noun ('companions OF …') or follows a preposition. As a plural it denotes a group, here in a possessive/linking relationship.
33.root: ص-ح-ب (ṣ-ḥ-b) — companionship, to accompany, keep company

34.meaning: 'The Fire' — fire, flame; in religious usage often the Fire of Hell, the blazing punishment of the Hereafter.
34.grammar: The definite article 'al-' ('the') plus the feminine noun 'nār' ('fire'). The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 'n' (so it is pronounced 'an-nār'). The '-i' ending is genitive, the case used after a preposition or to link the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the Fire').

1.meaning: Or who is it that…? — a compound particle fusing 'or' with 'who,' used to pose a contrasting rhetorical question: 'or rather, who…?'
1.grammar: Two particles merged: am ('or,' used to link question-alternatives) and man ('who,' for persons). Together they introduce a fresh alternative in a rhetorical question, contrasting one claim with another. Neither part inflects.

2.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
2.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

3.meaning: (Is) devoutly obedient — qānitun is an active participle meaning one who is constantly, humbly obedient and devoted to Allah.

parts.en: devoutly obedient, humbly devoted, standing in obedience

3.grammar: Form I active participle from root q-n-t, in the indefinite nominative (tanwīn ḍamma). Qunūt denotes deep, sustained obedience and devotion. The verse contrasts the one who is devoutly obedient through the night with one who is not.
3.root: ق-ن-ت (q-n-t) — to be devoutly obedient, to stand in devotion, to be humbly submissive

4.meaning: 'Hours / times / watches' — the plural of a word for a period or stretch of time, especially the hours of the night; moments or watches within a span of time.
4.grammar: A plural noun. The final -a ending is accusative; with words of time this case often signals 'during / at' a period (an adverbial sense of time), as well as marking a direct object more generally. The accusative -a is written on a supporting alif (ـاء).
4.root: ا-ن-ي (ʾ-n-y) — a time, period, the right moment

5.meaning: The night — the period of darkness from sunset to dawn.
5.grammar: Prefix 'al-' = 'the' (its 'l' merges with the word's initial 'l', said al-layl). A noun for night-time. The final -i is the genitive case ending, typically used after a preposition or to link to a preceding noun ('… OF the night').

6.meaning: Prostrating — sājidan is an active participle meaning one who is in prostration (sujūd), in the indefinite accusative as a circumstantial complement.

parts.en: prostrating, in a state of prostration

6.grammar: Form I active participle from root s-j-d, in the indefinite accusative (tanwīn fatḥa -an), used as a ḥāl describing the manner of worship — 'standing in obedience [while] prostrating'.
6.root: س-ج-د (s-j-d) — to prostrate, to bow down in worship

7.meaning: And standing — wa- is 'and'; qāiman is an active participle meaning 'one who is standing', referring to standing in prayer (qiyām).
7.grammar: Wa- is the coordinating conjunction. Qāim is Form I active participle from root q-w-m (to stand), in the indefinite accusative as a ḥāl. Together with sājidan, it describes the worshipper alternating between prostration and standing — the two key postures of ṣalāh.
7.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, to rise, to establish

8.meaning: Fearing — yaḥdharu is the imperfect third-person singular 'he fears', 'he is wary of', referring to fear of the Hereafter and Allah's punishment.

parts.en: he fears, he is wary, he is cautious

8.grammar: Form I imperfect verb (third masculine singular) from root ḥ-dh-r, meaning to be cautious, to fear, to beware. The doubling of the yāʾ (shaddah) in recitation indicates assimilation with the preceding wāw. Context: the devout servant fears the Hereafter.
8.root: ح-ذ-ر (ḥ-dh-r) — to be cautious, to fear, to beware of

9.meaning: A noun meaning 'the Hereafter / the next life / the world to come' — literally 'the last (abode)', the final, everlasting existence following this present life.
9.grammar: A definite noun (al- = 'the') bearing the -a ending, which marks the accusative (object) case — the form a noun takes when it is the object of a verb. It is feminine in form (the tā' marbūṭa ending).
9.root: ء-خ-ر (ʾ-kh-r) — to be last, to come after; lastness, the end

10.meaning: And hoping — wa- is 'and'; yarjū is the imperfect 'he hopes for', expressing hope alongside fear, the two wings of the believer's relationship with Allah.
10.grammar: Yarjū is Form I imperfect (third masculine singular) from root r-j-w, meaning to hope, to expect, to anticipate. The alif after the wāw is a spelling convention for the weak-ending verb. Together with yaḥdharu, it expresses the balanced state of the sincere believer: fearing punishment and hoping for mercy.
10.root: ر-ج-و (r-j-w) — to hope, to expect, to await with anticipation

11.meaning: (For the) Mercy — raḥmata is a noun meaning mercy, compassion, or grace (of Allah), in the accusative as the object of hoping.
11.grammar: Raḥma is a Form I noun from root r-ḥ-m, in the accusative (no tanwīn because it is in an iḍāfa/construct state — raḥmata Rabbihi, 'the mercy of his Lord'). It is the object of yarjū (he hopes for the mercy of his Lord).
11.root: ر-ح-م (r-ḥ-m) — to be merciful, to show compassion; mercy, womb

12.meaning: His Lord, Master, and Sustainer — the One who owns, nurtures, governs, and brings to completion; expressing both ownership and loving care over the one belonging to Him.
12.grammar: A masculine noun with an attached possessive pronoun ("his Lord"). The -i vowel on the noun is genitive, here drawn out because of the following possessive suffix -hi ("his"). The suffix -hi means "his," and its i-form follows naturally after an i-vowel.
12.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship, ownership, nurturing and sustaining to completion

13.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
13.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.
13.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, speak

14.meaning: An interrogative particle that turns a statement into a yes/no question, roughly "is it that…?" or "do…?". It can also carry a rhetorical or expectant tone rather than a literal request for information.
14.grammar: A question particle placed before a sentence to ask whether something is the case. It has no case ending and does not change form; it simply marks the words that follow as a yes/no question.

15.meaning: 'They are equal / it is the same' — to be on a par, level, or alike; to stand even with one another with no difference of value.
15.grammar: A Form VIII present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he/it is equal'). The 'ya-' prefix marks a present action; the weak final letter (from the root's last 'w/y') appears as the long ending. It expresses things being on the same level.
15.root: س-و-ي (s-w-y) — equality, levelness, being even/straight

16.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
16.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

17.meaning: They know, have knowledge, are aware. Expresses ongoing or habitual knowing held by a group of males (or a mixed group).
17.grammar: A present/future-tense verb. The ya- prefix with the -ūna ending means 'they' (a group of males). The full -ūna ending (rather than a shortened -ū) marks the indicative mood, signaling a plain statement of fact: 'they (do) know.'

18.meaning: 'And those who': a connective phrase introducing a specified group of people (masculine plural) about whom something will be said. It links them to what came before.
18.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'), which is masculine plural. A relative pronoun stands for a group and is normally followed by a clause describing them. Its form does not change for case; it stays alladhīna whatever its grammatical role.

19.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
19.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

20.meaning: They know, have knowledge, are aware. Expresses ongoing or habitual knowing held by a group of males (or a mixed group).
20.grammar: A present/future-tense verb. The ya- prefix with the -ūna ending means 'they' (a group of males). The full -ūna ending (rather than a shortened -ū) marks the indicative mood, signaling a plain statement of fact: 'they (do) know.'

21.meaning: 'Only / nothing but' — a restrictive particle that limits and emphasizes, asserting that the matter is exclusively so and no other ('it is only...'). It combines the emphatic 'inna' with the restricting 'mā'.
21.grammar: A compound particle formed from the emphatic inna ('indeed') and mā, which together work as a tool of restriction meaning 'only / nothing but'. It both stresses and confines the statement that follows to a single truth, excluding all alternatives.

22.meaning: He takes heed, calls to mind, reflects and is reminded. The verb conveys an inward act of recollection that leads to heeding admonition — letting a reminder sink in and bear fruit in awareness.
22.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, 3rd person masculine singular, of the reflexive 'tafaʿʿala' pattern (originally yatadhakkaru, with assimilation), which adds an inward, self-directed force ('to remind oneself'). The 'ya-' prefix marks 'he/it'; the '-u' ending marks the plain indicative, i.e. an ongoing or habitual action ('does / keeps doing').

23.meaning: 'Possessors of / owners of / people of' — a plural construct word meaning those endowed with or characterized by whatever follows it (e.g. 'those of understanding'). It has no singular of its own form and is always joined to a following noun.
23.grammar: A masculine plural noun used only in the construct state (always followed by another noun, 'possessors OF ...'). The -ū ending is the nominative plural form, marking it as the subject or doer of a sentence. The trailing alif is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.
23.root: — (a word for 'possessors of', having no verbal root)

24.meaning: The inner cores / kernels — figuratively, sound minds, understanding, or insight. Literally the plural of 'lubb,' the kernel or pith inside a shell; used of the discerning faculty of the heart, so 'people of the albāb' are those of genuine understanding and reflection.

parts.en: kernels / minds, understanding (broken plural of lubb)

24.grammar: A definite plural noun. The first segment الۡ (al-) is the definite article 'the.' Note that the word that follows already begins with its own alif-hamza: it is ʾalbāb, the broken (irregular) plural of lubb formed on the ʾafʿāl pattern, where that initial alif belongs to the plural template itself and is NOT a second definite article. So there is only one article here, prefixed to the intrinsic ʾalbāb. The final -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun in a possessive 'of …' relationship or follows a preposition or governing particle.
24.root: ل-ب-ب (l-b-b) — core, kernel, inner essence; hence sound intellect

1.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
1.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

2.meaning: O My slaves — yāʿibādi is a vocative address meaning 'O My servants/slaves', combining the vocative particle yā, ʿibādi (My servants), with the possessive yāʾ elided.

parts.en: My servants, My slaves (plural of ʿabd with first-person possessive)

2.grammar: Yā is the vocative particle. ʿIbādi is the broken plural of ʿabd (servant), with the first-person possessive yāʾ implied (ʿibādī → ʿibādi in pause/shortened form). This is a direct divine address to all human beings, or specifically to the believers, summoning them with intimacy.
2.root: ع-ب-د (ʿ-b-d) — to worship, to serve; a slave, a servant

3.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
3.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

4.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
4.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.
4.root: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — safety, security, trust, faith

5.meaning: Be mindful and wary of — guard yourselves by placing a protective barrier between yourselves and harm or wrongdoing. This is the verb of taqwā: God-conscious caution that shields one from what is forbidden.
5.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to a group ('you all'). The -ū ending directs the order to a masculine plural 'you.' Built on a reflexive pattern (Form VIII), it conveys 'protect yourselves / be on guard.'

6.meaning: Your Lord — the Master, Sustainer, and Nurturer who creates, owns, and cares for you, guiding His servants to completion. "Rabb" carries the joined senses of owner, sustainer, and the one who lovingly brings to maturity, here addressed to a group.
6.grammar: A masculine singular noun with an attached possessive "your" (plural addressee). The -a before the pronoun is the accusative case, which generally marks the word as the object of a verb (the thing being acted upon).
6.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, bring to completion

7.meaning: A compound meaning 'for those who' or 'belonging to those who'. It joins the preposition 'for/to' with a masculine plural relative pronoun ('those who'), introducing a clause that describes a group of people by something they do or possess.
7.grammar: The prefix 'li-' is a preposition meaning 'for', 'to', or expressing ownership/benefit ('belonging to'). The relative pronoun is 'alladhīna' ('those who'), but when 'li-' attaches to it the connecting hamza of 'al-' drops out and the two lām sounds merge into one doubled lām, so the form is written and read 'lilladhīna' rather than 'li-alladhīna'. 'alladhīna' has a fixed shape and does not change for case.

8.meaning: A verb meaning 'they did good / acted well / did beautifully'. The core sense ('iḥsān') is doing a thing excellently and beautifully, and also conferring kindness and benefit on others.
8.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in a derived (augmented) pattern meaning 'to do well, do good'. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they did…'). (The trailing silent alif is a spelling convention after plural -ū.)
8.root: ح-س-ن (ḥ-s-n) — to be good, beautiful, excellent

9.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
9.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
9.root: — (particle)

10.meaning: This (feminine) — a pointing word ('this one here') used for a single nearby thing that is grammatically feminine.
10.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun ('this') for a single feminine thing close at hand. It is fixed in form and does not change for case; it commonly precedes the noun it points to.

11.meaning: 'The nearer (life) / this world' — literally 'the nearest/lowest,' a name for the present worldly life as opposed to the Hereafter.
11.grammar: The definite article al- with dunyā, a feminine superlative/elative adjective ('the nearest, the lowest') used as a name for the present world. Its ending (alif maqṣūra) is invariable — it does not change for case — and it commonly describes 'the [worldly] life.'
11.root: د-ن-و (d-n-w) — nearness, being close or low; hence the 'near' present world

12.meaning: "A good thing / a benefit" — something good, beautiful, or pleasing; a good deed or a piece of good fortune.
12.grammar: A feminine singular noun/adjective. The -at ending marks it as feminine; the final -un is nominative case with tanwīn (the -n showing it is indefinite, 'a good thing'). The nominative typically marks the subject of a sentence.
12.root: ح-س-ن (ḥ-s-n) — goodness, beauty, excellence

13.meaning: And the earth — wa-arḍu is 'and the earth', referring to Allah's earth as spacious, i.e., there is no excuse for remaining in a land where one cannot worship Allah freely.
13.grammar: Wa- is the conjunction. Arḍ is a Form I noun from root ʾ-r-ḍ in the nominative (arḍu), here in the context of 'My earth is spacious'. The full verse states: 'Indeed My earth is spacious, so worship Me alone.'
13.root: أ-ر-ض (ʾ-r-ḍ) — the earth, the land, the ground

14.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
14.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

15.meaning: (Is) spacious / wide — wāsiʿatun is an adjective meaning vast, spacious, broad, used to describe Allah's earth as being wide enough to enable hijra (migration) for the sake of worship.
15.grammar: Form I active participle (wāsiʿa) from root w-s-ʿ, used as a predicate adjective, in the indefinite nominative (tanwīn ḍamma). The message: Allah's earth is so vast that no one should have an excuse for failing to worship Allah due to their location or circumstances.
15.root: و-س-ع (w-s-ʿ) — to be spacious, to be wide, to encompass

16.meaning: 'Only / nothing but' — a restrictive particle that limits and emphasizes, asserting that the matter is exclusively so and no other ('it is only...'). It combines the emphatic 'inna' with the restricting 'mā'.
16.grammar: A compound particle formed from the emphatic inna ('indeed') and mā, which together work as a tool of restriction meaning 'only / nothing but'. It both stresses and confines the statement that follows to a single truth, excluding all alternatives.

17.meaning: Will be paid back in full / will receive full recompense — yuwaffā is a passive verb meaning to be given in full, to receive complete reward.

parts.en: will be paid in full, will be given complete recompense

17.grammar: Form II passive imperfect (third masculine singular) from root w-f-y, meaning to fulfill or to pay in full. Yuwaffā indicates the patient ones will receive their reward completely and without any reduction. The alif maqṣūra marks the final weak root letter.
17.root: و-ف-ي (w-f-y) — to fulfill, to complete, to pay in full

18.meaning: The patient ones — al-ṣābirūna is the subject meaning those who endure with patience, the steadfast believers who persevere through trials.

parts.en: the patient ones, the steadfast, the persevering

18.grammar: Form I active participle (ṣābir) from root ṣ-b-r, in the definite nominative plural (ṣābirūna, masculine sound plural -ūna). It is the subject of yuwaffā: 'Indeed the patient ones will be paid their reward in full without reckoning.'
18.root: ص-ب-ر (ṣ-b-r) — to be patient, to persevere, to endure

19.meaning: Their reward, wage, or recompense — the due return given for work or deeds. The base word denotes earned payment or compensation, and the attached pronoun makes it 'their' (a group of males or a mixed group).
19.grammar: A noun in the object form: the -a ending (accusative) typically marks the word as the receiver of an action ('the reward' as the thing given). The suffix -hum means 'their / them' for a plural group.
19.root: أ-ج-ر (ʾ-j-r) — reward, wage, recompense for effort

20.meaning: 'Without' or 'other than' — the preposition bi- joined to ghayr, a noun meaning 'other than / not / lacking', together conveying the absence of something ('with no …', 'wrongfully').
20.grammar: bi- is a preposition that takes the genitive; ghayr is a noun of exception/negation ('other than'). Its -i ending is genitive (required after bi-) and it also links to a following noun in a possessive 'of' relationship, so 'bi-ghayri X' means 'without X / other than X'.
20.root: غ-ي-ر (gh-y-r) — otherness, difference, being other than

21.meaning: 'Reckoning / account / measure'. It refers to counting, calculating, or taking account — and by extension a limit or measure derived from counting. Often used of a tally or the act of holding to account.
21.grammar: The '-in' ending (tanwīn) marks the word as indefinite ('a reckoning / any measure') and in the genitive case. The genitive typically follows a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …').

1.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
1.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

2.meaning: 'Truly I' or 'indeed I' — the emphatic affirming particle inna ('truly, indeed, certainly'), which strengthens and confirms a statement, joined to the pronoun 'I'.
2.grammar: An emphasizing particle with an attached pronoun. 'Inna' is a particle of emphasis and affirmation that introduces a statement and lends it certainty ('it is certainly the case that…'). The attached -ī is the first-person singular pronoun ('I / me') in the object form this particle requires. Together: 'Indeed I…'.

3.meaning: 'I was commanded', 'I have been ordered / instructed'. It expresses that the speaker is the recipient of a command — someone else has issued an order and the speaker is bound by it.

parts.en: passive vowel: the action was done to the subject

3.grammar: Past-tense passive verb. The -tu ending means the subject is 'I', and the opening u-vowel makes it passive ('I was commanded' rather than 'I commanded'). The action is presented as completed.
3.root: ا-م-ر (ʾ-m-r) — to command, order, instruct

4.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
4.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'
4.root: — (particle; no root)

5.meaning: 'That I worship / serve' — to worship, to serve in humble devotion and obedience as a servant before his Master.
5.grammar: A present-tense verb. The a- prefix marks a first-person singular subject ('I'). The final -a is the subjunctive ending, taken when the verb is governed by a preceding particle (such as 'that/to'), giving the sense 'that I worship' or 'to worship'.

6.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
6.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

7.meaning: (Being) sincere — an active participle/adjective meaning one who is sincere, pure in intention, making religion exclusively for Allah alone.

parts.en: sincere, pure in devotion, making (religion) exclusively for Allah

7.grammar: Form IV active participle (mukhliṣ) from root kh-l-ṣ, in the indefinite accusative (tanwīn fatḥa -an), functioning as a ḥāl (circumstantial complement) — 'worshipping Him being sincere'.
7.root: خ-ل-ص (kh-l-ṣ) — to be pure, to be free from mixture, to be sincere

8.meaning: 'For it / for him / to it' — the preposition 'for/to' fused with the pronoun 'it/him,' conveying belonging, purpose, or direction toward something.
8.grammar: A prepositional phrase: the prefix li- ('for/to') joined with the pronoun -hu ('it/him'). It commonly expresses possession ('belonging to it'), benefit, or direction.

9.meaning: The dīn — a deep term covering religion, the way of life, the path of obedience and worship owed to Allah, and the reckoning/recompense for it; a complete system of belief and practice with accountability.
9.grammar: A definite noun ('al-' = 'the') with the -a (accusative) ending, which typically marks it as the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon) or the object of certain particles.
9.root: د-ي-ن (d-y-n) — religion, obedience, requital, debt/accountability

1.meaning: And I have been commanded — a past-tense statement in which the speaker reports being ordered or instructed by another; the doer of the commanding is left unnamed, so the focus rests on the speaker as the one under orders.
1.grammar: A past-tense passive verb with the prefixed 'wa' ('and'). The inner vowel pattern 'u-i' shows it is passive ('was commanded', no named commander), and the '-tu' ending makes the speaker its subject ('I was commanded').
1.root: ا-م-ر (ʾ-m-r) — commanding, ordering; an affair or matter

2.meaning: That — li-an is a compound particle meaning 'in order that', 'so that', expressing purpose.

parts.en: for, in order to (particle of purpose)

2.grammar: Li- is a particle of purpose/cause, and an is a subjunctive particle introducing a verbal clause. Together li-an introduces a purpose clause: 'I have been commanded to worship Allah, making the religion pure for Him, and I have been commanded in order that I be the first of the Muslims.'

3.meaning: '(that) I be / I should be' — the verb 'to be/become' in the first person, used in a dependent sense ('that I be…', 'lest I be…'). It expresses entering into or belonging to a described state.

parts.en: be / become (stem, ending in the subjunctive vowel -a)

3.grammar: A present-tense verb 'to be/become' with the 'I' prefix (a-). The stem ends in the third root letter ن, which carries the final short vowel -a; this -a is the subjunctive ending, the form used after particles such as 'that', 'so that', or 'lest' — so it reads 'that I be / I should be' rather than the plain statement 'I am' (which would end in -u).
3.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to become, to come into existence

4.meaning: First, foremost — the one that comes before all others in time, order, or rank.
4.grammar: A noun/adjective meaning 'first', here in a form that does not take normal indefinite case-tanwīn (a 'diptote'). The -a ending is accusative, marking it as an object or, very often, as the leading term of a possessive phrase ('the first of …').
4.root: أ-و-ل (ʾ-w-l) — to be first, to return to a beginning

5.meaning: The ones who submit/surrender — those who give themselves wholly to Allah in willing obedience and peace (the Muslims). As an active participle it names people characterized by this submission.
5.grammar: The prefix al- is 'the'. The stem is the Form IV active participle 'one who submits/surrenders'. The ending -īna is the sound masculine plural in the genitive/accusative state (the form used after prepositions, as object, or when linked to a preceding noun); its nominative counterpart would be -ūna. So: 'the ones who submit'.

1.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
1.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

2.meaning: 'Truly I' or 'indeed I' — the emphatic affirming particle inna ('truly, indeed, certainly'), which strengthens and confirms a statement, joined to the pronoun 'I'.
2.grammar: An emphasizing particle with an attached pronoun. 'Inna' is a particle of emphasis and affirmation that introduces a statement and lends it certainty ('it is certainly the case that…'). The attached -ī is the first-person singular pronoun ('I / me') in the object form this particle requires. Together: 'Indeed I…'.

3.meaning: I fear, I am afraid of, I stand in awe/dread — expressing the speaker's own fear, whether dread of harm or reverent awe.
3.grammar: A present-tense verb. The a- prefix marks the doer as 'I'. The final -u ending marks the ordinary (indicative) mood, used for a plain statement of an ongoing or habitual state ('I fear / I am fearing').
3.root: خ-و-ف (kh-w-f) — fear, fright, awe

4.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
4.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

5.meaning: 'I disobeyed', 'I rebelled against', 'I defied (an order)'. The verb means to go against a command and refuse obedience.
5.grammar: Past-tense verb. The -tu ending marks the subject as 'I' with the action completed: 'I disobeyed'. The stem comes from a root whose final letter is a weak letter, which surfaces here as 'ay' before the ending.

6.meaning: 'My Lord' — the Master, Sustainer and Nurturer, claimed in close personal relation by the speaker.
6.grammar: The noun rabb ('Lord') with the attached pronoun -ī meaning 'my'. This 'my' ending merges with the case-vowel of the noun, so a single long -ī is heard. The sense is 'the Lord who is mine'.
6.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to be lord/master, to nurture and sustain

7.meaning: Torment, punishment, or chastisement — severe, painful suffering imposed as a penalty.
7.grammar: A singular noun. The final -a (fatḥa) marks the accusative case, the form used for a direct object of a verb, or for the first noun of a possessive pair ('the punishment of …') when that whole phrase is itself an object.
7.root: ع-ذ-ب (ʿ-dh-b) — to torment, punish

8.meaning: a day — a day, the basic unit of daytime or a twenty-four-hour span; figuratively a time or occasion.
8.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The final -in ending marks the genitive case together with the indefinite 'a/an'. The genitive is the case used after prepositions or to link this noun to a preceding word ('… of a day').
8.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — a day, a span of time

9.meaning: An adjective meaning 'great', 'immense', 'mighty', or 'tremendous' — vast in size, importance, or gravity; used of things weighty and momentous.
9.grammar: An adjective on the intensive 'faʿīl' pattern (conveying a strong, established quality), carrying the genitive indefinite '-in' (tanwīn) ending. The genitive case typically appears after a preposition or when describing/qualifying a preceding genitive noun.
9.root: ع-ظ-م (ʿ-ẓ-m) — to be great, mighty, immense; (literally) bone, hence weightiness

1.meaning: 'Say!' — a command to utter or declare something aloud, addressed to a single male.
1.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to one male: 'say!'. Its natural form ends in a silent consonant (qul), but here a short -i vowel is added simply to smooth pronunciation before a following word that begins with a connecting sound; it carries no case meaning of its own.

2.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
2.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

3.meaning: I worship / I serve in devotion — to direct worship, obedience, and humble submission toward someone. The root carries the idea of being a devoted servant.
3.grammar: A present/future-tense verb. The a- prefix marks a first-person-singular subject ('I'). The final -u is the indicative ending, marking a plain statement of fact ('I worship / I do worship').
3.root: ع-ب-د (ʿ-b-d) — to worship, serve, submit as a devoted servant

4.meaning: (Being) sincere — an active participle/adjective meaning one who is sincere, pure in intention, making religion exclusively for Allah alone.

parts.en: sincere, pure in devotion, making (religion) exclusively for Allah

4.grammar: Form IV active participle (mukhliṣ) from root kh-l-ṣ, in the indefinite accusative (tanwīn fatḥa -an), functioning as a ḥāl (circumstantial complement) — 'worshipping Him being sincere'.
4.root: خ-ل-ص (kh-l-ṣ) — to be pure, to be free from mixture, to be sincere

5.meaning: A two-part phrase 'for Him' or 'to Him belongs,' expressing possession, ownership, or that something is due to one masculine being.
5.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('for/to/belonging to') with its vowel shifted to 'la-' before the pronoun. The attached -hu means 'Him', so the whole means 'for Him' or 'His'; the preposition signals possession or that something is owed or directed to that person.

6.meaning: My religion / my way of life — dīn denotes a complete system of belief, obedience, worship, and accountability to Allah; it also carries the senses of judgement and recompense. The attached -ī makes it 'my (dīn).'

parts.en: religion / way of obedience and recompense

6.grammar: A noun with the attached possessive pronoun -ī, 'my.' The case ending is masked because the noun is joined to this 'my' suffix.

1.meaning: So worship! — fa-uʿbudū is the plural imperative 'so worship (you all)', addressed to a group, commanding worship of Allah alone.
1.grammar: Fa- is a connective particle. Uʿbudū is the Form I imperative (second masculine plural) from root ʿ-b-d. The -ū ending marks the plural masculine imperative. This command follows the proof that Allah is the only one worthy of worship.

2.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
2.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

3.meaning: 'You wished / you willed' — to want, will, or desire something. Past tense, addressed to a group: 'you (all) wished'.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb. The suffix -tum marks the doer as a plural 'you (all)', giving 'you wished'. It denotes an act of will or desire. The stem carries a hamza (the glottal catch written ئ).
3.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-') — willing, wishing; (the same root gives the word 'thing')

4.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
4.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

5.meaning: Other than Him / apart from Him / besides Him. A relational word expressing the idea of being below, short of, or to the exclusion of something or someone.

parts.en: other than, apart from, besides, below

5.grammar: A relational noun/quasi-preposition meaning 'apart from / instead of'. It is followed by a possessive pronoun -hi ('Him'), which puts it in the genitive 'of' relationship; the kasra written under the pronoun reflects this genitive linkage.

6.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
6.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

7.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
7.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

8.meaning: "The losers / those who lose" — an active participle for those who suffer loss, who lose out or come to ruin, especially the ultimate loss of one's own soul.
8.grammar: An active participle in the masculine sound plural with the definite article 'the'. The -īna ending marks the accusative or genitive case — the form used when such a plural is a direct object, a predicate of 'to be', or follows a preposition (as opposed to the -ūna subject form).
8.root: خ-س-ر (kh-s-r) — to lose / suffer loss / be ruined

9.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
9.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

10.meaning: 'They lost', 'they have suffered loss', 'they ruined themselves' — said of a group of males who have come out as losers, forfeiting or wasting something of value, especially their own selves.
10.grammar: Past-tense verb. The -ū ending means the subject is 'they' (more than one male) and the action is presented as completed: 'they lost'.
10.root: خ-س-ر (kh-s-r) — loss, to lose, to suffer ruin

11.meaning: A noun meaning 'their own selves' or 'themselves' — the plural of 'nafs' (self, soul, person, inner self), joined to the pronoun 'their.' It commonly conveys the reflexive idea of acting upon one's own self.
11.grammar: A noun (a broken/irregular plural of 'nafs') with the attached possessive pronoun '-hum' ('their/them,' masculine plural). The -a case ending before the pronoun is accusative, typically marking the word as the direct object of a verb — i.e. the self upon which the action falls.
11.root: ن-ف-س (n-f-s) — self, soul, person; breath

12.meaning: And their families — wa-ahlīhim means 'and their families/households', referring to those saved along with the believers on the Day of Judgment.

parts.en: their (third person masculine plural possessive suffix)

12.grammar: Wa- is the conjunction. Ahl is a noun meaning family, household, or companions, in the genitive after a preceding verb or as an object. The suffix -him is third-person masculine plural possessive. Context: the wrongdoers will be told on Judgment Day of their loss — themselves and their families.
12.root: أ-ه-ل (ʾ-h-l) — family, household, people, those who belong to

13.meaning: The noun 'day' — a span of time, often used for a momentous Day or appointed time; in the accusative it frequently functions as 'on the day (when…)', marking the time at which something occurs.
13.grammar: A masculine noun bearing the -a (accusative) ending. As an adverb of time this ending typically gives the sense 'on the day…', fixing the moment of an event.
13.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, a period of time

14.meaning: "the Resurrection" — the standing-up of all people from death to be judged; literally the act of rising or standing up.
14.grammar: The al- prefix means "the." The -i ending (on the feminine -t) is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ("the … OF this") or follows a preposition.
14.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise

15.meaning: An opening particle of alert and emphasis — 'Now then!', 'Beware!', 'Truly!'. It calls attention to and strongly affirms the statement that follows.
15.grammar: An attention-drawing particle placed at the start of a statement. It rouses the listener and emphasizes what comes next, somewhat like 'Indeed!', 'Lo!', or 'Take note!' in English.

16.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
16.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

17.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
17.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

18.meaning: (Is) the loss — al-khusrānu is the definite noun meaning the (ultimate) loss, ruin, or failure, especially the loss of both this world and the Hereafter.

parts.en: the loss, the ruin, the total failure

18.grammar: Khusrān is a Form I verbal noun (maṣdar) from root kh-s-r, in the definite nominative, used as a predicate: 'that is the manifest loss'. It expresses complete and evident loss — losing both worldly and eternal life.
18.root: خ-س-ر (kh-s-r) — to lose, to suffer loss, to be in ruin

19.meaning: Clear, plain, manifest; that which makes things evident — both 'clearly apparent in itself' and 'making the truth clear to others'.
19.grammar: An active participle, 'the one that makes clear / the manifest', from a causative (form-IV) pattern, carried by the definite article al- ('the'). The final -u ending is the nominative case, the form used when the word serves as a subject or as a descriptor of such a word.

1.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
1.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

2.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
2.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

3.meaning: Above them / over them — the place or position over the top of someone or something, joined to 'them'.
3.grammar: A noun of place meaning 'above/over,' commonly used to mean 'over …'. The -i (kasra) is the genitive ending, here triggered by the following possessor; the attached '-him' is 'them' (its vowel is 'hi' after an -i sound).
3.root: ف-و-ق (f-w-q) — to be above; aboveness, superiority

4.meaning: Coverings / layers of shadow — ẓulalun is the plural of ẓulla, meaning canopies, coverings, or layers of shade, here referring to layers of fire above the wrongdoers in Hell.

parts.en: coverings, canopies, layers of shadow (or fire)

4.grammar: Ẓulal is a broken plural of ẓulla from root ẓ-l-l, in the indefinite nominative (tanwīn ḍamma). In this context it refers ominously to overlapping covers of fire (ṭabaqāt min al-nār) above and below the wrongdoers in Hell, a terrible inversion of the pleasant shade.
4.root: ظ-ل-ل (ẓ-l-l) — to shade, to cover; shade, canopy, layer

5.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
5.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

6.meaning: 'The Fire' — fire, flame; in religious usage often the Fire of Hell, the blazing punishment of the Hereafter.
6.grammar: The definite article 'al-' ('the') plus the feminine noun 'nār' ('fire'). The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 'n' (so it is pronounced 'an-nār'). The '-i' ending is genitive, the case used after a preposition or to link the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the Fire').

7.meaning: 'And from / and out of / and among.' A connector 'and' joined to the preposition 'from,' which marks origin, source, a starting point, or 'some of' a larger whole.
7.grammar: Two particles: the connector 'wa-' ('and') and the preposition 'min.' 'Min' indicates origin or source ('from'), a starting point, or partition ('some of'). Particles do not change their endings.

8.meaning: 'Beneath them / underneath them.' The noun taḥt means the lower side, the area below or under something, combined with an attached pronoun meaning 'them.'
8.grammar: A locational noun ('under') carrying the genitive -i ending, which appears here because it is followed by a possessor; the attached -him means 'them/their.' Together it reads 'the underneath of them' = 'beneath them.'
8.root: — (a fossilized locative adverb; not derived from a recognized triliteral root)

9.meaning: Coverings / layers of shadow — ẓulalun is the plural of ẓulla, meaning canopies, coverings, or layers of shade, here referring to layers of fire above the wrongdoers in Hell.

parts.en: coverings, canopies, layers of shadow (or fire)

9.grammar: Ẓulal is a broken plural of ẓulla from root ẓ-l-l, in the indefinite nominative (tanwīn ḍamma). In this context it refers ominously to overlapping covers of fire (ṭabaqāt min al-nār) above and below the wrongdoers in Hell, a terrible inversion of the pleasant shade.
9.root: ظ-ل-ل (ẓ-l-l) — to shade, to cover; shade, canopy, layer

10.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
10.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

11.meaning: A verb meaning 'he frightens', 'he makes (someone) afraid', or 'he puts fear into' — to instill dread or alarm in another. The doubled middle consonant gives it a causative, intensive sense ('to cause to fear').

parts.en: make afraid / frighten (Form II verb stem)

11.grammar: A present/future-tense Form II (faʿʿala) verb — the doubled middle root letter signals a causative/intensive meaning, here 'to cause to fear, to frighten'. The 'yu-' prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject, and the '-u' ending is the indicative mood, used for plain statements of ongoing or habitual action.
11.root: خ-و-ف (kh-w-f) — fear, fright, to be afraid

12.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
12.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.
12.root: — (proper divine name)

13.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
13.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

14.meaning: His servants/slaves; people regarded as devoted bondsmen wholly belonging to and dependent on their Master. The term conveys humble servitude and worshipful submission, not mere ownership.
14.grammar: A plural noun ('servants') with an attached possessive pronoun -hu ('his'). The -a vowel before the pronoun is the accusative ending, typically marking the word as the object of a verb. The plural ʿibād specifically connotes devoted worshippers in relation to their Lord.
14.root: ع-ب-د (ʿ-b-d) — worship, service, servitude

15.meaning: O My slaves — yāʿibādi is a vocative address meaning 'O My servants/slaves', combining the vocative particle yā, ʿibādi (My servants), with the possessive yāʾ elided.

parts.en: My servants, My slaves (plural of ʿabd with first-person possessive)

15.grammar: Yā is the vocative particle. ʿIbādi is the broken plural of ʿabd (servant), with the first-person possessive yāʾ implied (ʿibādī → ʿibādi in pause/shortened form). This is a direct divine address to all human beings, or specifically to the believers, summoning them with intimacy.
15.root: ع-ب-د (ʿ-b-d) — to worship, to serve; a slave, a servant

16.meaning: So be mindful of Me / so guard yourselves toward Me — a command to hold protective, God-conscious awareness (taqwā): to shield oneself from wrongdoing out of reverence.
16.grammar: The connective fa- ('so, then') joined to a plural command verb of the reflexive (ifta'ala) pattern, with an attached object 'me'. The -ū marks a masculine-plural addressee. The -ni is itself the complete first-person object pronoun 'me': the protective nūn (nūn al-wiqāya) has fused with the pronoun, and the final yā' is dropped in recitation, leaving -ni.
16.root: و-ق-ي (w-q-y) — to guard, shield, protect (the root of taqwā, God-consciousness)

1.meaning: 'And those who': a connective phrase introducing a specified group of people (masculine plural) about whom something will be said. It links them to what came before.
1.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'), which is masculine plural. A relative pronoun stands for a group and is normally followed by a clause describing them. Its form does not change for case; it stays alladhīna whatever its grammatical role.

2.meaning: (They) avoid / they shun — ijtanabū is a perfect verb meaning 'they avoided', 'they kept away from', referring to avoiding the worship of idols (ṭāghūt).

parts.en: they avoided, they shunned, they kept away from

2.grammar: Form VIII perfect verb (third masculine plural) from root j-n-b, meaning to stay away from, to avoid. The Form VIII pattern ifta'ala adds a sense of deliberate effort. Context: those who avoid the worship of false gods (ṭāghūt) and turn to Allah in repentance receive glad tidings.
2.root: ج-ن-ب (j-n-b) — to be aside, to avoid, to stay away from

3.meaning: 'The false god / idol / that which is wrongly worshipped' — a term (from the root meaning 'to overstep all bounds, transgress in tyranny') for any object of worship set up beside Allah: an idol, a tyrant, a devil, or any false deity that leads people into rebellion.

parts.en: false deity / idol / object of false worship

3.grammar: A noun made definite by al- ('the'). The final -a vowel marks the accusative case — the case typically taken by the direct object of a verb (the thing worshipped/served).
3.root: ط-غ-ي (ṭ-gh-y) — to exceed all limits, be tyrannical, transgress

4.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
4.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'
4.root: — (particle; no root)

5.meaning: They worship them — yaʿbudūhā means 'they worship them (feminine)', where the pronoun -hā refers to the idols (aṣnām, treated as feminine).

parts.en: them (feminine plural pronoun — referring to idols)

5.grammar: Yaʿbudū is Form I imperfect (third masculine plural) from root ʿ-b-d, in a relative clause. The suffix -hā is the third-person feminine singular pronoun, but used here for a non-rational plural (idols are treated grammatically as feminine singular). Context: contrasting those who avoided idols and those who worshipped them.
5.root: ع-ب-د (ʿ-b-d) — to worship, to serve, to be devoted to

6.meaning: And (they) turn (to Allah) / they repent — wa-anābū means 'and they turned back to Allah', expressing sincere repentance and return.

parts.en: they turned back (to Allah), they repented

6.grammar: Wa- is the conjunction. Anābū is Form IV perfect (third masculine plural) from root n-w-b, meaning to return, to repent, to turn back to Allah. The extended alif (hamza + alif) before the plural wāw is orthographic. Context: those who turned to Allah in repentance receive glad tidings.
6.root: ن-و-ب (n-w-b) — to return, to repent, to turn back to Allah

7.meaning: 'To / toward / up to' — a preposition marking the endpoint, goal, or limit of an action or motion: the direction something moves toward or the boundary at which it stops.
7.grammar: An invariable preposition. It has no case ending of its own but puts the noun that follows it into the genitive ('of / to' state). It indicates direction toward, or the terminal limit of, something.

8.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
8.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

9.meaning: To them / for them — the preposition li- ('to, for') joined to the pronoun 'them'. It expresses that something is directed toward, belongs to, or is for the benefit of a group.
9.grammar: The preposition li- ('to/for') combined with the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). When li- takes a pronoun its vowel becomes 'la-'. The final -u here is a connecting vowel added to ease pronunciation before a following word; it carries no case meaning of its own.

10.meaning: The glad tidings — good news, joyful announcement of something pleasing. The word names the very message of joy that brings cheer and makes the face brighten.
10.grammar: A feminine noun carrying the definite article al- ('the'). It ends in a fixed long -ā (the feminine pattern fuʿlā) which does not change for case, so the case is understood from context rather than a final short vowel.
10.root: ب-ش-ر (b-sh-r) — to bring good news, to rejoice

11.meaning: So give glad tidings! — fabashir is the imperative 'so give good news', addressed to the Prophet to deliver glad tidings to those who listen and follow the best of what they hear.

parts.en: give glad tidings! announce good news!

11.grammar: Fa- is a connective particle. Bashir is Form II imperative (second masculine singular) from root b-sh-r, meaning to give good news or glad tidings. The command is directed at the Prophet to announce reward to those who listen to speech and follow the best of it.
11.root: ب-ش-ر (b-sh-r) — to give glad tidings, to announce good news; skin, human

12.meaning: (To) My slaves — ʿibādi is a genitive noun meaning 'My servants', used after the command to give glad tidings (fabashir ʿibādi = give glad tidings to My servants).

parts.en: My servants, My slaves (with implied first-person possessive)

12.grammar: ʿIbādi is the broken plural of ʿabd in the genitive, with the first-person possessive yāʾ elided in pause form (ʿibādī → ʿibādi). It is the object of fabashir in an iḍāfa: 'give glad tidings to My servants.' The pause mark (ؙ) indicates a slight pause in recitation.
12.root: ع-ب-د (ʿ-b-d) — to serve, to worship; slave, servant

1.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
1.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

2.meaning: They listen, give ear, or pay attention; this verb pattern conveys actively and deliberately listening to something, lending one's ear rather than merely hearing in passing.
2.grammar: A present-tense verb in a reflexive/middle-voice (form VIII) pattern, which here adds the sense of taking in a sound for oneself — listening attentively rather than merely hearing. The prefix ya- marks a third-person ('he/they') subject, and the ending -ūna marks a male plural subject in an ongoing or habitual action: 'they listen / are listening.'

3.meaning: A noun meaning 'the speech, the saying, the utterance' — words that are spoken; a statement or what is said.
3.grammar: A verbal noun (the act/product of speaking) made definite by al- ('the'). The final -a ending is accusative, the case typically marking the direct object of a verb — the thing being acted upon.
3.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — saying, speaking

4.meaning: Then/so they follow, pursue, or go after; to take something as a thing to be imitated or adhered to. The verb implies actively following on behind and conforming to it.
4.grammar: A present/imperfect verb of the eighth form (which adds a sense of personally taking up the action of following). The opening fa- means 'so/then', linking it to what precedes. The ya-…-ūna frame marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'), and the -ūna ending is the indicative form used for an ongoing, unconditioned present action.
4.root: ت-ب-ع (t-b-ʿ) — to follow, pursue, come after

5.meaning: The best thereof — aḥsanahu means 'the best of it', referring to following the best meaning or interpretation when one hears speech or the Quran.

parts.en: the best of, the most excellent of
it (third person masculine singular object pronoun)

5.grammar: Aḥsana is Form IV elative (comparative/superlative — aḥsan, 'better/best') from root ḥ-s-n, in the accusative as the object of the preceding verb (yattabiʿūna = they follow). The suffix -hu is the object pronoun 'it'. Meaning: they listen to speech and follow the best of it.
5.root: ح-س-ن (ḥ-s-n) — to be good, beautiful, excellent; the best

6.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'those' — pointing to people or things that are distant or already known. It singles out a group ('those ones', 'it is those who').
6.grammar: A plural demonstrative pronoun, 'those'. It is fixed in form (no case endings). The -ka element signals distance/remoteness, pointing to something far off or notable. It can refer to people of either gender.

7.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
7.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

8.meaning: Allah has guided them — hadāhumu means 'He has guided them', with hadā (He guided) and -humu (them, accusative plural).

parts.en: them (third person masculine plural object pronoun)

8.grammar: Hadā is Form I perfect (third masculine singular) from root h-d-y, meaning to guide. The alif maqṣūra marks the weak verb ending. The suffix -humu is the third-person masculine plural object pronoun (with the connecting vowel -u). Context: those are the ones Allah has guided, and they are the people of understanding.
8.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — to guide, to lead to the right path

9.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
9.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.
9.root: — (proper divine name)

10.meaning: 'And those' — the connective 'and' joined to the demonstrative 'those'. It both links to what precedes and points out a group ('and it is those who…').
10.grammar: A connecting particle wa ('and') prefixed to a plural demonstrative pronoun, 'those'. The wa simply joins what follows to what came before. The demonstrative is fixed in form (no case endings), and its -ka element marks distance; it may refer to people of either gender.

11.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (referring to a group of males, or a mixed group). Because it stands on its own rather than being attached to a verb or noun, it often adds emphasis, singling out or stressing the subject ('they themselves', 'it is they who').
11.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It does not take case endings; the fixed -m simply marks the plural 'they'. Standing alone, it commonly serves to emphasise or isolate the subject.

12.meaning: 'Possessors of / owners of / people of' — a plural construct word meaning those endowed with or characterized by whatever follows it (e.g. 'those of understanding'). It has no singular of its own form and is always joined to a following noun.
12.grammar: A masculine plural noun used only in the construct state (always followed by another noun, 'possessors OF ...'). The -ū ending is the nominative plural form, marking it as the subject or doer of a sentence. The trailing alif is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.
12.root: — (a word for 'possessors of', having no verbal root)

13.meaning: The kernels, cores, or innermost parts — figuratively the faculties of sound reason and understanding, the discerning intellect that grasps the heart of a matter. The prefixed "al-" makes it definite ("the").
13.grammar: A definite plural noun (singular "lubb"). The '-i' ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ("… OF …") or follows a preposition. Here the genitive marks it as the thing possessed after a possessor-word.
13.root: ل-ب-ب (l-b-b) — core, kernel; sound understanding

1.meaning: An interrogative formed from three pieces meaning roughly 'Is then the one who…?' It opens a rhetorical question that compares two parties. The 'a-' is a question marker, 'fa-' links to a preceding statement and means 'then/so', and 'man' is the relative pronoun 'the one who / whoever'.
1.grammar: A combination of particles plus the relative pronoun 'man'. The leading 'a-' turns the sentence into a yes/no question (often rhetorical). 'fa-' is a connective meaning 'then/so', tying the question to what came before. 'man' refers to a person and introduces a clause describing them ('the one who…'); it does not change its ending for case.

2.meaning: Due right, just measure, rightful claim; that which is true and rightly owed — here used to mean 'as is truly its due'.
2.grammar: A noun meaning 'truth, right, due'. The final -a (accusative) often marks the object of a verb, and in a possessive phrase like this it commonly conveys the sense 'with the full right/due OF …', i.e. as something deserves to be done.
2.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, right, that which is due and real

3.meaning: A preposition fused with a pronoun, meaning 'upon him', 'on him', or 'toward him'. It marks the one to whom an action is directed or upon whom something rests.
3.grammar: The preposition 'upon/on' with an attached object pronoun -hi ('him', third-person masculine singular); its -i vowel is the regular form the pronoun takes after the 'y' sound. Paired with a verb of turning, this 'upon/toward him' marks the person the action reaches.

4.meaning: The word, statement, or decree — an utterance or pronouncement; when ascribed to Allah, a binding decree or settled promise that is sure to be fulfilled.
4.grammar: A feminine singular noun ('word, decree'). The ending -tu carries the feminine -t plus the nominative -u, which typically marks the word as the subject of a sentence or as the first term of a possessive phrase ('the word OF …').
4.root: ك-ل-م (k-l-m) — speech, a word, an utterance

5.meaning: The punishment, torment, or chastisement — severe penalty or suffering inflicted as retribution.
5.grammar: A singular masculine noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending is the genitive, which typically links it to a preceding noun ('… of the punishment') or follows a preposition.

6.meaning: An emphatic, rhetorical opener combining a question with the sense 'and/then'. It singles out the addressee ('you') and challenges them, roughly 'Is it then YOU who…?' — implying the answer is beyond the person's power.
6.grammar: Built on the question-particle a- ('is it/can it be…?') plus connective fa- ('and/then'), attached to the standalone pronoun anta, 'you' (one male). The pronoun carries no case ending; the fixed final -a is simply part of the word for 'you (masc. sg.)'. The whole expression poses a pointed, rhetorical question focused on the addressee.

7.meaning: (You can) save / rescue — tunqidhu is the imperfect second-person singular 'you save/rescue', used in a question implying impossibility.

parts.en: you save, you rescue, you deliver (from)

7.grammar: Form IV imperfect verb (second masculine singular) from root n-q-dh, meaning to rescue, to save, to deliver from danger. Used rhetorically: 'then can you save (afaanta tunqidhu) one who is already in the fire / destined for punishment?' — implying the Prophet cannot save those determined to disbelieve.
7.root: ن-ق-ذ (n-q-dh) — to save, to rescue, to deliver from danger

8.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
8.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.
8.root: — (pronoun)

9.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
9.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
9.root: — (particle)

10.meaning: 'The Fire' — fire, flame; in religious usage often the Fire of Hell, the blazing punishment of the Hereafter.
10.grammar: The definite article 'al-' ('the') plus the feminine noun 'nār' ('fire'). The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 'n' (so it is pronounced 'an-nār'). The '-i' ending is genitive, the case used after a preposition or to link the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the Fire').
10.root: ن-و-ر (n-w-r) — fire, blaze, burning

1.meaning: But, however, rather — a particle that sets off a correction or contrast with what came before, redirecting the statement.

parts.en: kasra of the light (reduced) particle form

1.grammar: A contrastive particle meaning 'but/however'. This is the light/reduced form of the emphatic لٰكِنَّ (lākinna): the doubled nūn is elided and the particle no longer governs a following noun. The final kasra (-i) belongs to the identity of this reduced form rather than being mere pronunciation liaison.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.
