3.meaning: 'They were mindful of Allah / guarded themselves'. This is the act of taqwā: being conscious of Allah, guarding oneself against wrongdoing out of reverence for Him, and shielding oneself from His displeasure. Past tense, masculine plural.

parts.en: to be mindful of Allah / guard oneself

3.grammar: This is a past-tense verb of the reflexive/intensive pattern (form VIII), conveying that the subjects actively guarded and protected themselves. The '-aw' (written ـوا) ending marks a masculine plural subject acting in completed past time ('they did').
3.root: و-ق-ي (w-q-y) — to guard, protect, shield

4.meaning: Their Lord, Master, and Sustainer — 'rabb' is the one who owns, nurtures, and brings a thing to its full development; with the attached pronoun, the Lord who is theirs.
4.grammar: A masculine noun with the possessive 'their' attached. The -a vowel before -hum marks the accusative case, the case typically used for the object of a verb.
4.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship, nurturing, mastery

5.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
5.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

6.meaning: (There are) lofty mansions / upper chambers — ghurafun is the plural of ghurfa, meaning upper rooms, high chambers, or elevated mansions in Paradise.

parts.en: lofty mansions, upper chambers, elevated rooms (in Paradise)

6.grammar: Ghuraf is the broken plural of ghurfa from root gh-r-f, in the indefinite nominative (tanwīn ḍamma). The verse describes Paradise as having lofty rooms built high, with rivers flowing beneath them — a description of the eternal reward for those who feared Allah.
6.root: غ-ر-ف (gh-r-f) — to scoop up; an upper room, a lofty chamber

7.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
7.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

8.meaning: Above them — fawqihā means 'above them', where fawqa (above) and -hā (them/it, referring to the chambers or their levels) describe the multi-tiered nature of the mansions.

parts.en: them, it (third person feminine pronoun — referring to the chambers)

8.grammar: Fawq is a noun used prepositionally meaning 'above', in the genitive after the implied preposition. The suffix -hā refers back to ghurafun (chambers) treated as a non-rational plural (feminine). The verse describes chambers built upon chambers — lofty multi-storied mansions.
8.root: ف-و-ق (f-w-q) — above, over, superior to

9.meaning: (There are) lofty mansions / upper chambers — ghurafun is the plural of ghurfa, meaning upper rooms, high chambers, or elevated mansions in Paradise.

parts.en: lofty mansions, upper chambers, elevated rooms (in Paradise)

9.grammar: Ghuraf is the broken plural of ghurfa from root gh-r-f, in the indefinite nominative (tanwīn ḍamma). The verse describes Paradise as having lofty rooms built high, with rivers flowing beneath them — a description of the eternal reward for those who feared Allah.
9.root: غ-ر-ف (gh-r-f) — to scoop up; an upper room, a lofty chamber

10.meaning: Built high / constructed — mabniyyatun is a passive participle meaning 'built', 'constructed', describing the lofty mansions as something that has been constructed.
10.grammar: Form I passive participle (maf'ūla pattern: mabniyya) from root b-n-y, meaning to build. Feminine singular indefinite nominative (tanwīn ḍamma), agreeing with ghuraf (chambers). It describes the rooms of Paradise as having been built/constructed — emphasizing their solidity and grandeur.
10.root: ب-ن-ي (b-n-y) — to build, to construct

11.meaning: A verb 'it flows, runs, streams' — used of water and rivers moving along, and of things that run or course freely. It describes continuous, ongoing motion.
11.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, 3rd person feminine singular. The ta- prefix here marks a feminine 'it/she' subject. The verb describes an ongoing or habitual action: 'it flows / keeps flowing.'
11.root: ج-ر-ي (j-r-y) — to flow, run, stream

12.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
12.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
12.root: — (preposition)

13.meaning: 'Beneath it / underneath it' — the noun for the underside or lower region of something, with an attached pronoun 'its' (referring to a feminine thing). It points to the space below or underneath a thing.
13.grammar: A location noun ('underneath') with the attached pronoun '-hā' ('its/her'), referring to a feminine noun. The -i ending is the genitive case, normally triggered here because words of place like 'under' commonly follow a preposition such as 'from' (min taḥti = 'from beneath').
13.root: ت-ح-ت (t-ḥ-t) — underneath, below

14.meaning: The rivers — al-anhāru is the definite plural of nahr (river), describing the rivers flowing beneath the dwellers of Paradise.
14.grammar: Anhār is the broken plural of nahr from root n-h-r, in the definite nominative (al-anhāru). It appears in the recurring Quranic description of Paradise: 'beneath which rivers flow' (tajrī min taḥtihā al-anhār).
14.root: ن-ه-ر (n-h-r) — a river; to flow, to scold

15.meaning: 'a promise / pledge' — a binding assurance of something to come; here as a noun naming the thing pledged or the act of pledging.
15.grammar: A verbal noun with the -a (accusative) ending, which typically marks it as a direct object or as an emphatic inner object reinforcing a verb of the same meaning ('a promise [truly promised]'). It names the act/content of promising.
15.root: و-ع-د (w-ʿ-d) — to promise, pledge, give an assurance

16.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
16.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

17.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
17.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

18.meaning: He breaks / fails to keep (a promise); He goes back on or leaves unfulfilled. From a verb whose core sense is 'to come after / be left behind', in this form meaning to default on a pledge or fail to deliver what was promised.
18.grammar: A present/future-tense verb. The yu- prefix marks the doer as 'he' (third-person masculine singular) and, in this vowel pattern, indicates a causative-type form. The final -u is the indicative ending, which marks the plain factual present ('he does / will do'), as opposed to moods that drop or change that vowel.
18.root: خ-ل-ف (kh-l-f) — to come after, succeed, be behind; hence to break a promise (leave it behind unfulfilled)

19.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
19.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

20.meaning: 'The appointed promise / the tryst / the pledged appointment' — a noun for a fixed promise or an appointed time and place agreed upon, with the definite article 'the'.
20.grammar: A definite noun. The final -a is the accusative case, which commonly marks the noun as the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon). The pattern denotes a fixed appointment or settled promise.
20.root: و-ع-د (w-ʿ-d) — to promise, appoint a time

1.meaning: 'Did not…?' — a particle combining a question with negation, used to ask 'Have I/has he not…?', often expecting agreement or serving as a gentle reminder.
1.grammar: An interrogative prefix 'a-' ('?') joined to the negation 'lam'. 'lam' negates a verb and places it firmly in the past ('did not'), and grammatically puts the following present-tense verb into the jussive (clipped) form. Together they form a rhetorical or confirming question.

2.meaning: You see, perceive, or take notice; to observe with the eye, or by extension to come to know or consider. Often used to draw attention, as in 'have you considered…?'
2.grammar: A present-tense verb addressed to a single male 'you,' marked by the 'ta-' prefix. The root's weak final letter has dropped, leaving the short final -a; this shortened form is the jussive/apocopated form, which appears after certain particles (such as 'did not' or in questions like 'have you not seen?').
2.root: ر-أ-ي (r-ʾ-y) — to see, perceive, consider, form an opinion

3.meaning: An emphatic particle meaning 'that' (as in 'I know that...') or 'indeed/surely.' It introduces a statement and gives it certainty and emphasis, presenting what follows as an established fact.
3.grammar: An emphatic particle that introduces a noun-clause ('that...'). It puts the following noun into the accusative case and lends the whole statement a sense of certainty and assertion. It typically comes after verbs of knowing, saying, or informing.

4.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
4.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.
4.root: — (proper name)

5.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'he sent down, he caused to descend, he revealed' — used especially of Allah sending down revelation, rain, or blessings from above.
5.grammar: A completed (past) action by a single masculine subject ('he'); the -a ending marks third-person masculine singular. The form IV (causative) pattern means 'to make something come down,' i.e., to send it down.

6.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
6.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

7.meaning: The sky or heaven — the canopy overhead; the expanse above the earth, also that which is elevated or raised over something. With the definite article it means 'the sky / the heaven'.
7.grammar: A noun with the definite article al- ('the'), in the genitive marked by the -i ending. (The 'l' of al- assimilates in sound into the following 's', a 'sun letter', though it is still written.) The genitive -i ending typically appears after a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …').
7.root: س-م-و (s-m-w) — height, loftiness; sky, heaven

8.meaning: 'water' — water in general, the fluid essential to life; also used for liquid such as rain. A basic noun for the substance of water.
8.grammar: An indefinite noun. The '-an' ending (tanwīn al-fatḥ) marks the accusative case together with indefiniteness — commonly the role of a direct object, the thing acted upon (e.g. what is sent down or brought).
8.root: م-و-ه (m-w-h) — water

9.meaning: And He makes it flow / and He channeled it — fasalakahu means 'then He caused it to pass through' or 'He made it travel', describing how Allah channels rain water through the earth.

parts.en: He caused to pass, He threaded through, He channeled

9.grammar: Fa- is the connective particle. Salaka is Form I perfect (third masculine singular) from root s-l-k, meaning to thread through, to travel, or to channel. The suffix -hu is the accusative object pronoun. Context: Allah sends rain down and then channels it through the earth as springs.
9.root: س-ل-ك (s-l-k) — to thread through, to travel, to make pass through

10.meaning: (As) springs — yanābīʿa is the plural of yanbūʿ, meaning springs of water, sources of water that gush from the earth.
10.grammar: Yanābīʿ is the broken plural (jamʿ al-takthīr) of yanbūʿ from root n-b-ʿ, in the indefinite accusative (fatḥa without tanwīn because it is a diptote — ghair munsarif). Context: after sending rain down and channeling it through the earth, Allah causes it to emerge as springs from which varied crops grow.
10.root: ن-ب-ع (n-b-ʿ) — to spring forth, to gush out; a spring of water

11.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
11.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
11.root: — (particle)

12.meaning: The earth; the land, ground, or soil. The world we walk upon, as opposed to the sky.
12.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('... of the earth') or follows a preposition (as after 'in / on the earth').
12.root: أ-ر-ض (ʾ-r-ḍ) — earth, land, ground

13.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
13.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

14.meaning: To bring out, produce, or cause to come forth — to make something emerge from where it was hidden or contained. The causative pattern means 'to make (something) go out'.

parts.en: brings forth / causes to come out

14.grammar: A present/future-tense verb, third-person masculine singular of the causative pattern: 'he/it brings forth'. The 'yu-' prefix marks 'he/it' and the causative vowel pattern adds the sense 'causes to come out'. The final '-u' marks the ongoing (indicative) mood — an action happening or habitual.
14.root: خ-ر-ج (kh-r-j) — going out, emerging

15.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
15.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

16.meaning: Sown crops, cultivated plants, or standing grain — vegetation deliberately planted and grown.
16.grammar: A verbal noun used concretely. The -an ending is accusative with nunation (the doubled 'n' sound), the case that typically marks the direct object of a verb — the thing acted upon or produced.
16.root: ز-ر-ع (z-r-ʿ) — to sow, plant, cause to grow

17.meaning: (Of) different (colors) — mukhtalifan is an active participle meaning 'varying', 'differing in kind', describing the varied colors and types of crops, fruits, and produce.
17.grammar: Form VIII active participle (mukhtalif) from root kh-l-f, in the indefinite accusative (tanwīn fatḥa -an), as a ḥāl or adjective describing the crops (zarʿ) produced — 'crops of different colors/types'. The form ifta'ala suggests inherent diversity or mutual difference.
17.root: خ-ل-ف (kh-l-f) — to differ, to vary, to come after

18.meaning: 'Its colors / its hues' — the various shades and tints belonging to a single thing, with the attached pronoun pointing back to the masculine thing that possesses them.
18.grammar: A plural noun (of lawn, 'color') with an attached possessive pronoun. The -u ending (nominative) typically marks it as a subject; the attached -hu means 'its/his', referring to a single masculine owner.

19.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
19.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

20.meaning: They wither / it withers — yahīju is an imperfect verb meaning to become dry, to wither, to dry out (said of plants).

parts.en: it withers, it dries out, it becomes parched

20.grammar: Form I imperfect verb (third masculine singular) from root h-y-j, meaning to be agitated, to dry out, to wither. The -ū final form is suppressed. In context it describes the vegetation: first green and lush, then it withers and turns yellow — a parable of the transience of this world.
20.root: ه-ي-ج (h-y-j) — to become agitated, to dry and wither, to stir up

21.meaning: And you see it — fatarāhu means 'then you see it'; fa- connects to the previous verse, tarā is 'you see', and -hu is the object pronoun 'it'.

parts.en: it (object pronoun, referring to the vegetation)

21.grammar: Fa- is the connective particle. Tarā is Form I imperfect (second masculine singular) from root r-ʾ-y, with the alif maqṣūra final (weak verb). The suffix -hu refers to the vegetation (zarʿ). The verse describes the life cycle: green → yellowing → withering — as a parable of the world's transience.
21.root: ر-أ-ي (r-ʾ-y) — to see, to observe, to perceive

22.meaning: Turn yellow — muṣfarran is a passive participle meaning 'yellowed', 'turned yellow', describing the vegetation after it withers.
22.grammar: Form IV passive participle (muṣfarr, from iṣfarra — to turn yellow) from root ṣ-f-r, in the indefinite accusative (tanwīn fatḥa -an) as a ḥāl describing the state of the vegetation. The shaddah on the rāʾ indicates the doubled root letter. It depicts the yellowing stage of plants before they become dry chaff.
22.root: ص-ف-ر (ṣ-f-r) — to be yellow, to turn yellow; the color yellow

23.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
23.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

24.meaning: He makes them (into) / He turns it — yajʿaluhu means 'He makes it' or 'He renders it', with Allah as the subject making the vegetation into dry debris.

parts.en: He makes, He renders, He turns (into)
it (object pronoun — referring to the vegetation)

24.grammar: Yajʿalu is Form I imperfect (third masculine singular) from root j-ʿ-l, meaning to make, to render, or to cause to become. The suffix -hu is the accusative object pronoun. The verse states that after yellowing, Allah turns it into ḥuṭām (dry debris/chaff) — completing the parable of worldly life.
24.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, to render, to place, to cause to be

25.meaning: Crushed, dried-up fragments — broken, withered stubble or chaff; plant matter reduced to brittle, shattered debris.
25.grammar: An indefinite noun. The -an ending combines the accusative case (which commonly marks a direct object or the result of an action — '… into debris') with indefiniteness ('some/debris in general').
25.root: ح-ط-م (ḥ-ṭ-m) — to smash, crush, break to pieces

26.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
26.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

27.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
27.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

28.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
28.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

29.meaning: Surely (it is) a reminder — ladhikrā is an emphatic statement meaning 'indeed it is a reminder', 'truly it is a remembrance/admonition'.

parts.en: a reminder, a remembrance, an admonition

29.grammar: The lām is the emphatic particle (lām al-ibtidāʾ or lām al-tawkīd). Dhikrā is a feminine noun (Form I verbal noun) from root dh-k-r, meaning a reminder or admonition, with the alif maqṣūra marking. It refers to the Quran or the parable just given as a reminder for people of intellect.
29.root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — to remember, to mention; a reminder, remembrance

30.meaning: For those of understanding — li-ulī is a compound meaning 'for those who possess', and al-albāb (implied from context) means 'sound minds/intellects'.

parts.en: those who possess, those endowed with (construct plural)

30.grammar: Li- is the preposition of benefit. Ulī is an irregular noun meaning 'those who possess' or 'those endowed with', always in the construct state (iḍāfa), from root ʾ-l-w/ʾ-w-l. It is followed by al-albāb (minds) in context: li-ulī l-albāb — 'for those possessed of sound minds/intellects'.
30.root: أ-ل-و (ʾ-l-w) — to possess; ulī: those who have/possess

31.meaning: The inner cores / kernels — figuratively, sound minds, understanding, or insight. Literally the plural of 'lubb,' the kernel or pith inside a shell; used of the discerning faculty of the heart, so 'people of the albāb' are those of genuine understanding and reflection.

parts.en: kernels / minds, understanding (broken plural of lubb)

31.grammar: A definite plural noun. The first segment الۡ (al-) is the definite article 'the.' Note that the word that follows already begins with its own alif-hamza: it is ʾalbāb, the broken (irregular) plural of lubb formed on the ʾafʿāl pattern, where that initial alif belongs to the plural template itself and is NOT a second definite article. So there is only one article here, prefixed to the intrinsic ʾalbāb. The final -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun in a possessive 'of …' relationship or follows a preposition or governing particle.
31.root: ل-ب-ب (l-b-b) — core, kernel, inner essence; hence sound intellect

1.meaning: An interrogative formed from three pieces meaning roughly 'Is then the one who…?' It opens a rhetorical question that compares two parties. The 'a-' is a question marker, 'fa-' links to a preceding statement and means 'then/so', and 'man' is the relative pronoun 'the one who / whoever'.
1.grammar: A combination of particles plus the relative pronoun 'man'. The leading 'a-' turns the sentence into a yes/no question (often rhetorical). 'fa-' is a connective meaning 'then/so', tying the question to what came before. 'man' refers to a person and introduces a clause describing them ('the one who…'); it does not change its ending for case.

2.meaning: He opened up, expanded, or laid open - most often used of opening or expanding the chest/breast, an image for making someone receptive, relieved, and at ease.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he opened/expanded'). The a-a-a vowel pattern is the basic active past form. The final -a is the standard ending of a completed past-tense action performed by 'he'.
2.root: ش-ر-ح (sh-r-ḥ) - to open up, expand, lay open, make spacious

3.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
3.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.
3.root: — (proper divine name)

4.meaning: A noun meaning 'his chest' or 'his breast' — the seat of the heart, used figuratively for the inner self, one's capacity for feeling, courage, and receptivity.
4.grammar: A noun carrying the -a (accusative) ending, which typically marks it as the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon) or the subject of certain constructions. The attached -hu is the possessive pronoun 'his'.
4.root: ص-د-ر (ṣ-d-r) — chest, front, that which proceeds forth

5.meaning: A phrase meaning 'to Islam' / 'for submission' — Islam being wholehearted submission and surrender to Allah, the willing entrusting of oneself to His will.
5.grammar: Built from the preposition li- ('to / for') joined to the noun with the definite article al-. The final -i (genitive) ending appears because the noun follows a preposition; this case typically signals 'of', 'to', or 'for' relationships.

6.meaning: A two-part phrase: the connector 'then / so' plus the standalone pronoun 'he / it,' used to point back and resume with 'then he…' or 'so it…'
6.grammar: The connector 'fa' ('then/so') plus the detached subject pronoun 'huwa' ('he/it'), 3rd-person masculine singular. Both are indeclinable, with no case ending; the pronoun typically begins or emphasizes a statement about 'he/it.'

7.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
7.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

8.meaning: A light — nūrin is a noun meaning light, radiance, or guidance, in the indefinite genitive after a preposition.
8.grammar: Nūr is a Form I noun from root n-w-r, in the indefinite genitive (tanwīn kasra -in). In context it refers to the light that Allah places in the heart of one He guides, or to the spiritual illumination that comes with guidance — 'Is one whose breast Allah has opened to Islam and he is upon a light from his Lord…?'
8.root: ن-و-ر (n-w-r) — to shine, to illuminate; light, radiance

9.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
9.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

10.meaning: A phrase meaning 'his Lord'. 'Lord' (rabb) denotes the Master, Owner, Sustainer, and Nurturer who creates, provides for, and governs — far richer than a mere title; here joined to 'his'.
10.grammar: The noun 'Lord' with the genitive -i ending followed by the attached pronoun -hi ('his'). The genitive case appears because the noun is linked to a preceding word ('… OF his Lord') or follows a preposition. The lengthened -hī reflects how this pronoun is pronounced after an -i vowel.
10.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship, nurturing, ownership, sustaining and bringing to completion

11.meaning: 'So woe …' — a connective 'so/then' plus 'woe': an exclamation of impending doom, ruin, or grievous distress called down upon someone. It is a cry of warning and lament, not a literal noun of place.
11.grammar: The connective fa- ('so / then') prefixed to the noun 'woe.' The noun stands in the nominative with indefinite marking (the -un ending, tanwīn). Used this way it functions as an exclamation — 'woe (be) to …' — typically followed by 'to/for' someone.
11.root: و-ي-ل (w-y-l) — woe; ruin, doom, grievous distress

12.meaning: To (those whose hearts are) hardened — lil-qāsiyati is a genitive phrase meaning 'for those who have hardened (hearts)', the preposition and definite feminine active participle.

parts.en: for the, to the (preposition + definite article)
the hardened ones (feminine genitive), those with hard hearts

12.grammar: Li- is the preposition, with the definite article al- assimilated. Qāsiya is a Form I active participle (feminine) from root q-s-w, meaning hard, harsh, unfeeling. In the genitive after li-. The full reference is lil-qāsiyati qulūbuhum: 'for those whose hearts are hardened (against the remembrance of Allah).'
12.root: ق-س-و (q-s-w) — to be hard, harsh, unfeeling; hardness of heart

13.meaning: 'Their hearts' — the hearts belonging to a masculine plural group. In Qur'anic usage the 'heart' is the seat of understanding, intention, feeling, and faith, not merely the physical organ.
13.grammar: A plural noun ('hearts') in the nominative, shown by the -u before the pronoun, which typically marks it as the subject of a sentence. The attached 'hum' means 'their' (a group of males or mixed group), giving 'their hearts.'
13.root: ق-ل-ب (q-l-b) — heart; to turn over, fluctuate

14.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
14.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

15.meaning: Remembrance, recollection, calling to mind; also mention, invocation, or the very words by which something is brought to mind and kept present.
15.grammar: A verbal noun ('remembrance, mention'). The final -i ending is the genitive case: it typically links the word to a following noun in a possessive or 'of' relationship, or marks it as the object of a preceding preposition ('from/of remembrance').
15.root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — to remember, to mention, to call to mind

16.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
16.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

17.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'those' — pointing to people or things that are distant or already known. It singles out a group ('those ones', 'it is those who').
17.grammar: A plural demonstrative pronoun, 'those'. It is fixed in form (no case endings). The -ka element signals distance/remoteness, pointing to something far off or notable. It can refer to people of either gender.

18.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
18.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

19.meaning: Means 'straying / error / being lost' — wandering off the right path, the opposite of guidance, whether literally losing one's way or going astray in belief and conduct.
19.grammar: An abstract noun: 'straying / error.' The -in ending is the genitive with 'tanwīn' (the -n marking it indefinite) — the case a noun takes after a preposition or in a possessive link, e.g. 'in an error.' The long -ā- belongs to this noun-pattern.
19.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to stray, go astray, lose the way

20.meaning: Means 'clear / plain / making manifest' — something that is evident in itself and also makes other things plain, leaving no ambiguity.
20.grammar: An active participle (a 'doer' noun) from a pattern that often carries the sense 'making clear' as well as 'being clear.' The -in ending is the genitive with 'tanwīn' (the -n marking it indefinite), the form taken after a preposition or when describing a genitive noun — i.e. it agrees with a preceding indefinite noun in the genitive ('a clear …').
20.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — to be clear, distinct; to make evident

1.meaning: Allah — the proper name of the One God, the sole and absolute Deity worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a name, not a common noun, and refers to the Creator and Sustainer of all that exists.
1.grammar: The proper divine name. The final -u ending is nominative, the case typically marking the subject (the doer) of a sentence or the noun being identified.

2.meaning: A verb meaning 'he sent down / brought down', especially in stages or portions. The Form II shape adds intensity or gradualness to the basic 'descend', hence 'to send down piece by piece'.
2.grammar: Past-tense (perfect) verb, third-person masculine singular, Form II. The doubled middle letter marks the intensive/gradual sense; the final -a is the standard ending for a completed past-tense action done by 'he'.
2.root: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — to descend, come down, send down

3.meaning: A verb meaning 'he did good / acted well, excellently' — to do what is beautiful, fine, and right; also 'he was good (at something)'.
3.grammar: A Form IV (afʿala) past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular 'he'; the bare -a ending marks a completed action by 'he'. Form IV here gives the sense of doing/making good, acting with excellence.
3.root: ح-س-ن (ḥ-s-n) — goodness, beauty, excellence

4.meaning: The speech/account/narration — a piece of talk, a report, story, or statement; that which is related or told. With 'the', it points to a particular discourse or account.
4.grammar: A noun with the definite article 'al-' ('the'). The final -i is the genitive case — the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… OF …'). The pattern faʿīl gives a thing-told sense: an account or narration.
4.root: ح-د-ث (ḥ-d-th) — to happen anew; to relate, narrate, recount

5.meaning: 'A writing / a prescribed decree' — that which is written down; by extension a fixed ordinance, an appointed term, or a binding decree.
5.grammar: An indefinite noun in the accusative case: the -an ending (the 'an' sound with nunation) marks the object of a verb or a related role, and signals an indefinite 'a writing/decree'. The pattern 'kitāb' is the verbal noun denoting a written thing.

6.meaning: (Its parts) resembling each other — mutashābihan is an active participle meaning 'resembling each other', 'consistent', describing the Quran's internal consistency and harmony.

parts.en: resembling each other, mutually consistent, similar in style

6.grammar: Form VI active participle (mutashābih) from root sh-b-h, in the indefinite accusative (tanwīn fatḥa -an) as a ḥāl describing the Quran. The Form VI tafāʿala expresses mutual resemblance. The Quran is described as mutashābihan mathāniya — 'consistent (in its parts), oft-repeated'.
6.root: ش-ب-ه (sh-b-h) — to resemble, to be similar; resemblance, likeness

7.meaning: Oft-repeated — mathāniya is a plural noun meaning 'repeated', 'reiterated', describing the Quran's themes and verses as oft-repeated for emphasis and reminder.
7.grammar: Mathānī is the broken plural of mathnā or from root th-n-y, meaning to fold, to repeat, to double. In the indefinite accusative (without tanwīn as it is a diptote). It describes the Quran's characteristics: its themes of mercy and warning, its stories and teachings, are repeated throughout for emphasis — a hallmark of its unique style.
7.root: ث-ن-ي (th-n-y) — to fold, to repeat, to double; oft-repeated

8.meaning: (The skins) shiver / quiver — taqshaʿirru is an imperfect verb meaning to shudder, to get goosebumps, to bristle with awe and fear.

parts.en: shiver, shudder, get goosebumps (out of awe/fear)

8.grammar: Form XI imperfect verb (third feminine singular) from root q-sh-ʿ-r, meaning to bristle, to shudder, to get goosebumps. The Form XI (ifʿalalla) is used for colors and defects becoming established. Here it describes the physical reaction of the skins (julūd) of the believers when they hear the Quran — a sign of deep awe and reverence.
8.root: ق-ش-ع-ر (q-sh-ʿ-r) — to shudder, to bristle, to get goosebumps (quadrilateral root)

9.meaning: 'From it / out of it / from him'. It combines the preposition 'from / out of' with the pronoun 'it/him'.
9.grammar: The preposition min ('from / out of', indicating origin or source) with the attached pronoun -hu ('it' / 'him'), referring to a singular masculine thing or person. As object of the preposition, the pronoun is in the oblique form.
9.root: — (no triliteral root; a preposition with a pronoun)

10.meaning: (The) skins — julūdu is the plural of jild, meaning skins or hides, referring to the physical skin of the believers that shudders upon hearing the Quran.
10.grammar: Julūd is the broken plural of jild from root j-l-d, in the nominative as the subject of taqshaʿirru (the skins shiver). The verse describes the physical and spiritual response of believers to the Quran: first their skins shiver, then both their skins and hearts soften at the remembrance of Allah.
10.root: ج-ل-د (j-l-d) — the skin, the hide; to flog; endurance

11.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
11.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

12.meaning: 'They fear' or 'they hold in awe' — experiencing khashya, a fear mixed with reverence and awareness of someone's greatness, especially the kind of dread that comes from knowledge of the one feared.
12.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb. The -awna ending marks a masculine-plural 'they' subject (the long final root-vowel blends into the plural ending) and the indicative mood, which states the action as an ongoing or habitual fact.
12.root: خ-ش-ي (kh-sh-y) — fear blended with awe and reverence

13.meaning: Their Lord, Master, and Sustainer — 'rabb' is the one who owns, nurtures, and brings a thing to its full development; with the attached pronoun, the Lord who is theirs.
13.grammar: A masculine noun with the possessive 'their' attached. The -a vowel before -hum marks the accusative case, the case typically used for the object of a verb.
13.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship, nurturing, mastery

14.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
14.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

15.meaning: (They) relax / they soften — talīnu is an imperfect verb meaning to become soft, to relax, to become supple — the opposite of shivering/bristling.

parts.en: they soften, they relax, they become supple

15.grammar: Form I imperfect verb (third feminine plural in agreement with the non-rational plural julūd) from root l-y-n, meaning to be soft, to soften, to become gentle. It describes the second stage: after the initial shudder of awe, the believers' skins (and hearts) soften at the remembrance of Allah — a full and balanced spiritual response.
15.root: ل-ي-ن (l-y-n) — to be soft, to soften, to become gentle

16.meaning: Their skins — the outer coverings of the body, belonging to a group of males. It is the plural of 'skin' joined to a possessor 'them'.
16.grammar: A plural noun in the possessed (construct) state. The -u ending marks the nominative case, typically the case of the subject of a sentence. The attached -hum means 'their' (third-person masculine plural), making the whole 'their skins'.
16.root: ج-ل-د (j-l-d) — skin, hide; (also the act of flogging the skin)

17.meaning: And their hearts — waqulūbuhum is 'and their hearts', with wa- (and) and qulūb (hearts, plural of qalb) and -hum (their).
17.grammar: Wa- is the conjunction. Qulūb is the broken plural of qalb from root q-l-b, in the nominative as an additional subject. The possessive -hum is third-person masculine plural. The verse says both their skins and their hearts soften (talīnu julūduhum waqulūbuhum) at the remembrance of Allah.
17.root: ق-ل-ب (q-l-b) — the heart; to turn, to flip

18.meaning: A preposition meaning 'to,' 'toward,' or 'up to' — pointing to the end-point, goal, or limit of a motion, direction, or extent.
18.grammar: A preposition (a small linking word). It governs the noun after it, putting that noun in the genitive case, and points to a destination or limit ('to,' 'toward,' 'as far as').

19.meaning: Remembrance, recollection, calling to mind; also mention, invocation, or the very words by which something is brought to mind and kept present.
19.grammar: A verbal noun ('remembrance, mention'). The final -i ending is the genitive case: it typically links the word to a following noun in a possessive or 'of' relationship, or marks it as the object of a preceding preposition ('from/of remembrance').
19.root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — to remember, to mention, to call to mind

20.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
20.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

21.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
21.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

22.meaning: Guidance; right direction and true leading — being shown and set upon the correct way (construct form, 'guidance of …').
22.grammar: A verbal noun ending in a long -ā from a weak-final root. Its form (without the article and ending in -ā) commonly serves as the first term of a possessive phrase ('the guidance OF …'). It names the abstract idea of being rightly guided.
22.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — to guide, lead rightly, show the way

23.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
23.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

24.meaning: 'He guides / leads on the right way' — to show someone the correct path, direct them rightly, or lead them to a goal, whether literally or in matters of belief and conduct.
24.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular: the ya- prefix means 'he'. The verb ends in a long -ī (a weak final letter); in this indicative form the long vowel stands in place of the usual -u mood marker, still conveying a plain, ongoing statement ('he guides').
24.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — guidance, showing the way, leading rightly

25.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
25.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

26.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
26.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

27.meaning: A present-tense verb meaning 'he wills, he wishes, he chooses' — to want or intend something by one's own decision.
27.grammar: A present/ongoing action by a single masculine subject ('he'); the ya- prefix marks third-person masculine singular, and the final -u marks the indicative mood — a plain statement of fact ('he wills'), as opposed to a command or a verb governed by 'that.'
27.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʾ) — willing, wishing; the root behind 'thing' (shayʾ)

28.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
28.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

29.meaning: He lets/leads astray — he causes someone to lose the right way, leaving them to wander from guidance.
29.grammar: A present-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular ('he …'), in the causative pattern ('to cause to stray'). It stands in the jussive/conditional mood (the doubled lām broken apart and given a helping -i to ease pronunciation), typically meaning 'whomever he lets stray …'.
29.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to stray, go astray, lose the way

30.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
30.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

31.meaning: A two-part expression: 'so/then' joined to a negating word 'not.' The first piece links to what precedes (drawing a result or sequence), and the second negates the statement that follows. Together roughly: 'so… not / and so it did not…'
31.grammar: A connective particle fa- ('so, then,' showing result or sequence) plus the negating particle mā. When mā precedes a past-tense verb, it denies that the action happened ('did not…').

32.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
32.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

33.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
33.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

34.meaning: A guide — one who shows the way, leads to the right path, or directs others toward what is correct. The indefinite form conveys 'any guide' or 'a guide (at all)'.
34.grammar: An active participle ('one who guides'). It belongs to the class of nouns ending in a weak letter, so the indefinite tanwīn shows up as -in. This -in marks it as indefinite and signals nominative/genitive case: 'a guide'.
34.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — to guide, lead rightly, direct

1.meaning: An interrogative formed from three pieces meaning roughly 'Is then the one who…?' It opens a rhetorical question that compares two parties. The 'a-' is a question marker, 'fa-' links to a preceding statement and means 'then/so', and 'man' is the relative pronoun 'the one who / whoever'.
1.grammar: A combination of particles plus the relative pronoun 'man'. The leading 'a-' turns the sentence into a yes/no question (often rhetorical). 'fa-' is a connective meaning 'then/so', tying the question to what came before. 'man' refers to a person and introduces a clause describing them ('the one who…'); it does not change its ending for case.

2.meaning: Will shield / will protect — yattaqī is an imperfect verb from the root w-q-y meaning to protect oneself, to shield from, to use as a guard against.

parts.en: he will shield (himself), he will protect (himself with)

2.grammar: Form VIII imperfect verb (third masculine singular) from root w-q-y, meaning to guard, to shield, to protect oneself. In context it describes the wretched person who tries to shield himself from the torment of Judgment Day using his own face — the worst of fates, as there is no protection then.
2.root: و-ق-ي (w-q-y) — to protect, to guard, to shield from harm

3.meaning: With his face — biwajhihi means 'with his face', where bi- is the instrument preposition 'with' and wajh is 'face' and -hi is 'his'.
3.grammar: Bi- is the preposition of instrument or means. Wajh is a noun from root w-j-h meaning face, direction, aspect, in the genitive after bi-. The suffix -hi is the third-person masculine singular possessive. Context: the wrongdoer on Judgment Day will try to shield himself from punishment using only his face — there is nothing else left to protect him.
3.root: و-ج-ه (w-j-h) — the face, the direction; to face, to direct toward

4.meaning: Evil, harm, or grievousness — the bad or distressing aspect of something; in a possessive link, 'the worst of …' or 'a grievous …'.
4.grammar: A singular masculine noun in the accusative (-a ending), which typically marks an object of a verb or the first term of a possessive link ('the evil OF …'). The sense is 'grievous / worst kind of.'
4.root: س-و-ء (s-w-ʾ) — evil, harm, to be bad

5.meaning: The punishment, torment, or chastisement — severe penalty or suffering inflicted as retribution.
5.grammar: A singular masculine noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending is the genitive, which typically links it to a preceding noun ('… of the punishment') or follows a preposition.

6.meaning: The noun 'day' — a span of time, often used for a momentous Day or appointed time; in the accusative it frequently functions as 'on the day (when…)', marking the time at which something occurs.
6.grammar: A masculine noun bearing the -a (accusative) ending. As an adverb of time this ending typically gives the sense 'on the day…', fixing the moment of an event.
6.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, a period of time

7.meaning: "the Resurrection" — the standing-up of all people from death to be judged; literally the act of rising or standing up.
7.grammar: The al- prefix means "the." The -i ending (on the feminine -t) is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ("the … OF this") or follows a preposition.
7.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise

8.meaning: And it was said — a statement was uttered or a command was given (by an unnamed speaker).
8.grammar: A past-tense passive verb. The internal vowel pattern (qīla, with 'ī') marks it as passive — the doer is unspecified, so it means 'it was said' rather than 'he said.' The final '-a' is the standard ending of a third-person masculine singular past verb.
8.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, speak, utter

9.meaning: A prepositional phrase, 'for/to the wrongdoers' — al-ẓālimūn being those who do wrong or injustice, who put things out of their rightful place; in religious usage especially those who wrong their own souls through disbelief or transgression.
9.grammar: A definite active participle (a 'doer' noun, 'those who wrong') in the masculine plural, governed by the preposition li- ('for, to'). The plural ending -īna is the genitive/accusative plural form, required here after the preposition. The single written lām after li- is the definite article 'the', its own letter merged into the preposition.
9.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — to do wrong, oppress; injustice

10.meaning: Taste! / experience it firsthand — a command to undergo and feel something directly, as one tastes food. Often used of being made to feel a consequence.
10.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to a group: 'taste!' The -ū ending marks the addressee as masculine plural ('you all'). From a hollow root whose middle letter appears as a long ū in this form.
10.root: ذ-و-ق (dh-w-q) — to taste, to experience directly

11.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
11.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

12.meaning: A past-tense verb of 'being' addressed to a group: 'you (all) were', 'you (all) used to be'. From kāna, the core verb 'to be'. With a following predicate it often means 'you were (in a state of) …' or 'you used to …'.
12.grammar: This is a past-tense verb. The '-tum' suffix is the attached subject marker for a masculine plural 'you all'. Since the doer is built into the suffix, the verb stands in its base past form ('you all were').
12.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

13.meaning: To earn, acquire, or gain through one's own effort — to perform deeds (good or bad) and so accrue their consequences. It carries the sense of actively working for and bringing upon oneself a result.
13.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb. The 'ta-…-ūna' frame marks a second-person masculine plural subject — 'you all' do or are doing the action. The '-ūna' ending signals the plural 'you' and that the verb is in its full (indicative) form, describing an action that is real and ongoing.
13.root: ك-س-ب (k-s-b) — to earn, acquire, gain by effort

1.meaning: A verb meaning 'he denied / cried lies against / rejected as false' — to treat something or someone as a lie, refusing to accept it as true and openly rejecting it.
1.grammar: Past-tense verb (form II, intensive), third-person masculine singular ('he denied / rejected as false'). The doubled middle letter (kadhdhaba) gives the sense of actively declaring something false. The final -a is the past-tense ending for a masculine singular doer.
1.root: ك-ذ-ب (k-dh-b) — to lie; (form II) to deny, to call a lie

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
3.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
3.root: — (preposition)

4.meaning: 'Before them' in time — denoting what came earlier, the period or persons preceding a masculine plural group.
4.grammar: An adverb of time, 'before,' carrying the genitive ending -i because it is linked to a following possessor. The attached 'him' means 'them' (a group of males or a mixed group), giving 'before them.' The -i ending reflects that the word is governed in a possessive link.
4.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to precede, come before; before/prior

5.meaning: So came upon them — fa-atāhumu means 'then it came to them' — describing the punishment of Hell coming upon the wrongdoers.

parts.en: them (third person masculine plural object pronoun)

5.grammar: Fa- is the connective. Atā is Form I perfect (third masculine singular) from root ʾ-t-y/w-t-y, meaning to come, to arrive. The alif maqṣūra marks the third-singular perfect. The suffix -humu is the third-person masculine plural object pronoun. Context: the punishment came upon them from where they did not expect.
5.root: أ-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come, to arrive, to bring

6.meaning: "the punishment / torment" — a painful penalty or chastisement inflicted as retribution; suffering imposed as a consequence.
6.grammar: The al- prefix means "the." The -u ending is nominative, the case that typically marks the subject of a verb or the doer/topic of a sentence.

7.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
7.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
7.root: — (preposition)

8.meaning: Wherever / in whatever place — an adverb pointing to an unspecified location, 'in the place where ...'.
8.grammar: An invariable adverb of place ('where / wherever'). Although it ends in -u, it is fixed in form and does not change for case; it is normally followed by a clause stating the situation tied to that place.

9.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
9.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

10.meaning: A verb meaning 'they perceive / they are aware / they sense.' The root denotes fine, immediate awareness — noticing or feeling something, often subconsciously. It frequently appears in the negative, expressing that people fail to realize something.

parts.en: perceive / sense / be aware (Form I stem)

10.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, Form I (imperfect stem yashʿuru, with -u- after the second root letter), third-person masculine plural. The prefix 'ya-' and ending -ūna give 'they (masc.) do / are doing,' the -ūna marking the indicative — an ongoing or habitual state of awareness (or, when negated, the lack of it).
10.root: ش-ع-ر (sh-ʿ-r) — to perceive, sense, be finely aware

1.meaning: So Allah made them taste — fa-adhāqahumu means 'then He caused them to taste'; adhāqa is Form IV of dhāqa (to taste), meaning to cause someone to taste/experience.

parts.en: He made (them) taste, He caused (them) to experience

1.grammar: Fa- is the connective. Adhāqa is Form IV perfect (third masculine singular) from root dh-w-q, meaning to cause to taste. The Form IV causative makes another experience something. The suffix -humu is the masculine plural object pronoun. Context: Allah made the wrongdoers taste humiliation in this life and greater punishment in the Hereafter.
1.root: ذ-و-ق (dh-w-q) — to taste, to experience; to cause to taste

2.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
2.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

3.meaning: Disgrace and humiliation — public shame, abasement, and the lowering of one's standing; a state of being brought low and dishonored.
3.grammar: A definite noun ('the disgrace'). The -a ending marks the accusative case, typically identifying the noun as the direct object of a verb or otherwise placed in that case.
3.root: خ-ز-ي (kh-z-y) — to be disgraced, humiliated, put to shame

4.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
4.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
4.root: — (particle)

5.meaning: 'The life' — living existence, the state of being alive.
5.grammar: The definite article al- with the feminine noun ḥayāt ('life'); the waw belongs to the stem and the tā' marbūṭa is its feminine suffix. The final -i is the genitive case vowel, which typically marks the word as following a preposition or standing in an 'of' relationship to a following noun.

6.meaning: 'The nearer (life) / this world' — literally 'the nearest/lowest,' a name for the present worldly life as opposed to the Hereafter.
6.grammar: The definite article al- with dunyā, a feminine superlative/elative adjective ('the nearest, the lowest') used as a name for the present world. Its ending (alif maqṣūra) is invariable — it does not change for case — and it commonly describes 'the [worldly] life.'
6.root: د-ن-و (d-n-w) — nearness, being close or low; hence the 'near' present world

7.meaning: Severe suffering, torment, or punishment inflicted as chastisement. The prefixes add emphasis and definiteness: 'and surely the punishment …'.
7.grammar: A noun with the -u (nominative) ending, the case used for a sentence's subject. The la- prefix is an emphatic 'surely/indeed', and wa- is 'and'. Together: 'and surely the punishment …'.
7.root: ع-ذ-ب (ʿ-dh-b) — to torment, punish, cause pain

8.meaning: The Hereafter — the final, lasting life that comes after death and the present world; literally 'the last/latter (abode or life)', as opposed to the first, nearer life.
8.grammar: A feminine adjective used as a noun, with 'the'. The -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF …'), or follows a preposition or oath particle.
8.root: ء-خ-ر (ʾ-kh-r) — to be last, to come after, end

9.meaning: Greater, bigger, more grave — the comparative/superlative 'more great' or 'greatest'.
9.grammar: An elative on the afʿal pattern, expressing 'more/most great'. Such forms are diptotes, so they take -u (without nunation) in the nominative; the -u marks it as a subject or predicate ('is greater').
9.root: ك-ب-ر (k-b-r) — greatness, bigness

10.meaning: A conditional particle introducing a hypothetical or contrary-to-fact supposition: 'if (it were the case that…)'. It typically presents a condition that is unfulfilled or merely imagined, often implying the result did not or would not happen.
10.grammar: An indeclinable particle (no case ending). It signals a hypothetical 'if': it sets up a supposed condition whose consequence is then stated, frequently with the sense 'if X were so, then Y would be so' — often where X is contrary to fact.

11.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
11.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
11.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

12.meaning: They know, have knowledge, are aware. Expresses ongoing or habitual knowing held by a group of males (or a mixed group).
12.grammar: A present/future-tense verb. The ya- prefix with the -ūna ending means 'they' (a group of males). The full -ūna ending (rather than a shortened -ū) marks the indicative mood, signaling a plain statement of fact: 'they (do) know.'
12.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — to know; knowledge

1.meaning: "And indeed / and most certainly" — combines 'and' with the emphatic 'la-' and the particle 'qad'; before a past-tense verb 'qad' affirms that the action has definitely and already happened, reinforced into 'and indeed it surely did'.
1.grammar: The conjunction 'and' plus the emphatic 'la-' ('surely') plus the particle 'qad'. With a past-tense verb, 'qad' stresses that the act is real and completed ('has indeed happened'); together they form a strong oath-like affirmation. These are function words and are not inflected.

2.meaning: We have set forth — ḍarabnā means 'We struck' or 'We set forth', used idiomatically with mathal to mean 'We have given a parable/example'.

parts.en: We have set forth, We have given (a parable); We struck

2.grammar: Form I perfect verb (first plural) from root ḍ-r-b, meaning to strike, to beat, to set forth. The phrase ḍarabnā mathal (We have set forth a parable) is a standard Quranic idiom. The -nā suffix is the first-person plural (royal/majestic plural for Allah).
2.root: ض-ر-ب (ḍ-r-b) — to strike, to beat; to set forth (a parable/example)

3.meaning: To the people, for mankind — addressed or directed toward human beings in general; 'an-nās' is the collective word for 'people, humankind'.
3.grammar: The preposition 'li-' (to/for) joined to 'an-nās' (the people); the article's 'a' drops in pronunciation and its 'l' assimilates into the noun's 'n' (shown by the doubling). The -i ending is the genitive case, required because the word follows the preposition 'li-'. 'nās' is a collective noun for humankind with no singular of its own root form.
3.root: ن-و-س / ا-ن-س (n-w-s / ʾ-n-s) — humankind, people

4.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
4.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
4.root: — (particle)

5.meaning: 'This' — a pointing word (demonstrative) used for something near, masculine singular: 'this one (here).' It singles out a specific, present thing.
5.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun, masculine singular, for something near at hand ('this'). It is fixed in form and does not change for case. It points out a particular thing and can stand alone ('this') or precede a noun ('this X').

6.meaning: The Qur'an — the recited Revelation; literally 'the Recitation/Reading,' the Book sent down to be recited aloud.
6.grammar: A verbal noun meaning 'recitation/reading,' used as the proper name of the Book, with the definite article al- ('the'). The final -i is the genitive ending: it typically follows a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …').

7.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
7.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
7.root: — (preposition)

8.meaning: 'every,' 'each,' or 'all' — a word expressing totality or completeness. It indicates the entirety of something: when joined to a singular indefinite noun it means 'every (single) one,' and when joined to a definite noun it can mean 'all of' or 'the whole of.'
8.grammar: A noun of totality. The final '-i' ending is genitive (the 'of/possession' case): it marks the word as governed by a preceding preposition or as the first term of a possessive link to a following noun, so it typically reads 'of every…' or 'every…' leading into what follows.
8.root: ك-ل-ل (k-l-l) — totality, comprising the whole

9.meaning: A likeness, parable, or illustrative example — a comparison or proverb-like case set forth to make a truth vivid and clear; mathal denotes a similitude or model instance.
9.grammar: A noun meaning 'a similitude/parable/example.' The final -in (tanwīn kasra) is the indefinite genitive ending, which appears after a preposition or in a possessive link, and the absence of 'the' shows it is indefinite ('a parable / some example').
9.root: م-ث-ل (m-th-l) — to resemble, be like; hence likeness, example, parable

10.meaning: A compound particle of hopeful expectation, meaning roughly 'perhaps', 'so that', or 'in the hope that'. It expresses a wished-for or anticipated outcome — when used of people, an expectation that they might do or become something. The attached pronoun specifies the ones concerned: 'they' (a group).

parts.en: perhaps / so that / in hope that

10.grammar: The particle laʿalla governs a following noun or pronoun in the accusative-style attachment; the suffix -hum is the attached pronoun 'they/them', here naming the group about whom the hope or expectation is expressed.

11.meaning: 'They take heed / call to mind / reflect and remember' — to bring something back to mind and be admonished by it, to wake up to a reminder.
11.grammar: Present/future tense verb on a reflexive, effortful pattern ('to make oneself remember, to be admonished'). The ya- prefix marks third person and the -ūna ending makes it masculine plural ('they do'), describing ongoing action. The full -ūna ending shows it is in the normal indicative form.
11.root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — to remember, to mention, to call to mind

1.meaning: A recitation, a reading; a text meant to be recited aloud. As a common noun it denotes 'something recited,' and as a proper name it is the Qur'an, the recited Scripture.
1.grammar: A verbal noun meaning 'recitation.' The ending -an is accusative with nunation (the -n marking it indefinite, 'a recitation'); the accusative is the case typically marking the object of a verb or a noun being specified.

2.meaning: An adjective meaning 'Arabic' — pertaining to the Arabs or to their language; that which is in clear, eloquent Arabic speech.
2.grammar: A relational adjective formed with the -iyy suffix ('belonging to / characterized by'). The final -an (tanwīn) is the indefinite accusative: it marks an indefinite descriptive word agreeing with an indefinite accusative noun it qualifies ('an Arabic …').

3.meaning: 'Other than / different from / not'. A noun used to express difference or negation — 'something other than X', and so 'not-X'. It functions to exclude or contrast with what follows.
3.grammar: A noun of difference/exception. The -a ending marks the accusative case, the form it takes when it serves as a direct object or as a descriptive substitute standing in an object position; it governs a following noun in the genitive ('other than …'). That it takes case endings and tanwīn confirms it is a true noun, not a particle.
3.root: غ-ي-ر (gh-y-r) — to be other, different; otherness, change

4.meaning: Possessor of / the one having — a relational word meaning 'owner of' or 'endowed with,' used to attach a quality or relationship to the noun it describes.
4.grammar: A relational noun meaning 'owner/possessor of,' which must be followed by another noun ('possessor OF …'). It declines for case: dhū (nominative), dhī (genitive), dhā (accusative). The form dhī (ending -ī) is its genitive, used when it follows a preposition or describes a preceding genitive noun. It never stands alone; it always governs a following noun.
4.root: — (a relational noun meaning 'possessor of'; no verbal root)

5.meaning: Crookedness / deviation — ʿiwajin is a noun meaning bend, crookedness, or distortion, in the indefinite genitive, denying any such defect in the Quran.
5.grammar: ʿIwaj is a Form I noun from root ʿ-w-j, meaning a bend or crookedness, in the indefinite genitive (tanwīn kasra -in). Used in a negation: 'a Book with no ʿiwaj in it' — meaning the Quran is straight, consistent, and free from any distortion or contradiction.
5.root: ع-و-ج (ʿ-w-j) — to be crooked, bent, deviated; crookedness

6.meaning: A compound particle of hopeful expectation, meaning roughly 'perhaps', 'so that', or 'in the hope that'. It expresses a wished-for or anticipated outcome — when used of people, an expectation that they might do or become something. The attached pronoun specifies the ones concerned: 'they' (a group).

parts.en: perhaps / so that / in hope that

6.grammar: The particle laʿalla governs a following noun or pronoun in the accusative-style attachment; the suffix -hum is the attached pronoun 'they/them', here naming the group about whom the hope or expectation is expressed.

7.meaning: They are mindful of Allah / they guard themselves; to live in reverent awareness that shields one from wrongdoing (the verb behind taqwā).
7.grammar: A Form VIII present-tense verb. The ya-…-ūna frame means 'they (do)' for a group of males, with the final -na marking the indicative mood — a plain statement of an ongoing or habitual reality.
7.root: و-ق-ي (w-q-y) — to protect, shield, guard against harm

1.meaning: He struck / set forth — literally 'to hit', but commonly used in the sense of putting forward or coining a likeness or example.
1.grammar: Past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he'), shown by the bare stem with its final -a. So: 'he struck' or 'he set forth (an example)'.
1.root: ض-ر-ب (ḍ-r-b) — to strike, hit; to set forth, coin (a likeness)

2.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
2.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

3.meaning: 'A likeness / example / parable / comparison.' A noun denoting something put forward as an illustration or analogy — a similitude that clarifies a point by comparison. It can also mean a proverb or a model case.
3.grammar: A noun. The -an ending is the indefinite accusative, the case used for the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon); the doubled 'n' sound (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('an example / some likeness').
3.root: م-ث-ل (m-th-l) — likeness, similarity, to resemble; example, model

4.meaning: A man — rajulan is a noun meaning 'a man', in the indefinite accusative, used in a parable comparing one who has multiple masters to one who has a single master.
4.grammar: Rajul is a Form I noun from root r-j-l, in the indefinite accusative (tanwīn fatḥa -an). In this verse, the parable: 'Allah sets forth the example of a man shared among multiple quarreling partners, and another man belonging exclusively to one man — are they equal?'
4.root: ر-ج-ل (r-j-l) — a man, a male person; foot

5.meaning: 'In it / in him' — the preposition 'in, inside, within' joined to a pronoun referring to a single masculine or neuter thing. It locates something inside or as part of that referent.
5.grammar: A preposition with an attached object pronoun.
