The pronoun -hi refers to one masculine (or grammatically masculine) thing and stands as the object of the preposition; its vowel is -i because attached pronouns take that shape after the long -i of fi. Together they answer 'in what?' or 'in whom?'.

6.meaning: 'Partners' / 'associates' / 'sharers' — the plural of 'partner', those who jointly share in something (such as property, ownership, or a claim).
6.grammar: A masculine plural noun (the broken plural of شَرِيك 'partner') on the pattern afʿilāʾ. The -u ending is the nominative case, marking it as the subject or the thing being identified ('partners'); this plural pattern does not take nunation.

7.meaning: Quarreling (with each other) — mutashākisūna is a plural active participle meaning 'quarreling', 'arguing with each other', 'in dispute'.

parts.en: quarreling, disputing, arguing with each other (plural active participle)

7.grammar: Form VI active participle (mutashākis) from root sh-k-s, in the definite or indefinite nominative plural (-ūna). Form VI expresses mutual action. Shaks means difficulty or contrariness; mutashākisūn are partners who are in conflict with each other over the man — a parable for the polytheist who has multiple false gods versus the monotheist who has only Allah.
7.root: ش-ك-س (sh-k-s) — to be contrary, difficult; to quarrel with one another

8.meaning: And a man — warajulan is 'and a man', the second subject in the parable — the man belonging exclusively to one master.
8.grammar: Wa- is the conjunction introducing the second half of the parable. Rajulan is repeated from the first part, again in the indefinite accusative. This second man, as opposed to the first, belongs entirely to one master — a parable for the sincere monotheist whose worship is devoted to Allah alone.
8.root: ر-ج-ل (r-j-l) — a man, a male person

9.meaning: (Belonging) exclusively — salaman means 'in peace', 'entirely/exclusively for one', describing the second man as belonging wholly to one master.

parts.en: exclusively (belonging to one), entirely for one, at peace

9.grammar: Salam (also read silm) is a noun from root s-l-m meaning peace, wholeness, or exclusive belonging. In the indefinite accusative (tanwīn fatḥa -an) as a ḥāl or predicate adjective. It describes the second man as being wholly dedicated/belonging to a single master — contrasted with the man shared among quarreling partners.
9.root: س-ل-م (s-l-m) — peace, wholeness, submission; to be safe and whole

10.meaning: To one man — lirajulin means 'belonging to one man', 'for a single man', completing the parable of the second slave.
10.grammar: Li- is the preposition of possession/belonging. Rajulin is the indefinite genitive (tanwīn kasra -in). The pause mark (ؕ) indicates a stop in recitation. Together: 'a man exclusively belonging to one master' — the second half of the parable illustrating tawhid vs. shirk.
10.root: ر-ج-ل (r-j-l) — a man, a male person

11.meaning: An interrogative particle that turns a statement into a yes/no question, roughly "is it that…?" or "do…?". It can also carry a rhetorical or expectant tone rather than a literal request for information.
11.grammar: A question particle placed before a sentence to ask whether something is the case. It has no case ending and does not change form; it simply marks the words that follow as a yes/no question.

12.meaning: 'The two of them are equal / are alike' — two things being on the same level, matching one another.
12.grammar: A present-tense verb (form VIII, 'iftaʿala') meaning 'to be/become equal'. The 'ya-' prefix marks third person, and the '-āni' ending is the dual, meaning 'the two of them' do the action. The retained final 'ni' shows the verb is in its base (indicative) state.
12.root: س-و-ي (s-w-y) — equality, evenness, being level

13.meaning: 'A likeness / example / parable / comparison.' A noun denoting something put forward as an illustration or analogy — a similitude that clarifies a point by comparison. It can also mean a proverb or a model case.
13.grammar: A noun. The -an ending is the indefinite accusative, the case used for the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon); the doubled 'n' sound (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('an example / some likeness').
13.root: م-ث-ل (m-th-l) — likeness, similarity, to resemble; example, model

14.meaning: All praise, commendation, and grateful acknowledgement — the recognition that beauty, goodness, and perfection rightly belong to and are owed to the one being praised. As a definite noun with the article 'al-', it conveys that the totality of praise is encompassed.
14.grammar: A definite noun (carrying the article 'al-', 'the'). The final '-u' ending is nominative: it marks the word as the subject or main topic of a statement — the thing being talked about or the doer of an action, rather than its object.
14.root: ح-م-د (ḥ-m-d) — to praise, to commend, to give thanks

15.meaning: A two-part word: the preposition 'li-' meaning 'to', 'for', or 'belonging to', attached to the name 'Allah'. It conveys 'to Allah' or 'for Allah'.
15.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('to/for') pulls the following noun into the genitive case, which is why 'Allah' ends in '-i' (llāhi). The '-i' ending is the regular result of a noun governed by a preposition.

16.meaning: A particle of retraction meaning 'rather,' 'no, but,' or 'nay' — it cancels or sets aside what was just said and shifts to a corrected or contrasting statement that follows.
16.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it never changes form). Its function is to redirect the discourse: it dismisses a prior idea and introduces what is actually the case.

17.meaning: Most of them / the greater part of them — the noun 'akthar' (the greater number, the majority), built on a comparative/superlative pattern of k-th-r ('much/many'), with the pronoun 'them'.
17.grammar: A noun in possessive (genitive) construction: 'aktharu' ('the most of') plus the attached pronoun '-hum' ('them') yields 'most of them'. The '-u' on 'akthar' is the nominative ending, typical when this phrase serves as the subject.
17.root: ك-ث-ر (k-th-r) — to be much, many, numerous

18.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
18.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

19.meaning: They know, have knowledge, are aware. Expresses ongoing or habitual knowing held by a group of males (or a mixed group).
19.grammar: A present/future-tense verb. The ya- prefix with the -ūna ending means 'they' (a group of males). The full -ūna ending (rather than a shortened -ū) marks the indicative mood, signaling a plain statement of fact: 'they (do) know.'

1.meaning: 'Indeed you' — an emphasis particle meaning 'truly / indeed' joined to the pronoun 'you', used to open a statement with certainty and stress about the person addressed.
1.grammar: The emphasis particle 'inna' ('indeed, truly') with an attached pronoun. 'inna' adds strong assertion to a sentence and grammatically governs the following noun/pronoun in the accusative. The suffix '-ka' means 'you' (masculine singular) as its subject.

2.meaning: Will die — mayyitun is a noun/adjective meaning 'one who will die', 'mortal', or 'already dead', addressing the Prophet that he like all humans is mortal.
2.grammar: Form I active participle with intensive pattern (mayyit, from root m-w-t) in the indefinite nominative (tanwīn ḍamma). Used as a predicate in a nominal sentence addressing the Prophet: 'Indeed, you are mortal and indeed they are mortal' — establishing the universality of death.

3.meaning: And indeed, they — wa-innahum is a compound meaning 'and indeed they', introducing an emphatic statement about the disbelievers also being subject to death.

parts.en: they (third person masculine plural pronoun — subject of inna)

3.grammar: Wa- is the conjunction. Inna is the emphatic particle that takes a nominal subject in the accusative. Hum is the accusative pronoun subject of inna. The verse addresses the Prophet: 'You will die and they (the disbelievers) will also die' — all will face judgment.
3.root: (particles: wa- conjunction; inna emphatic; hum pronoun)

4.meaning: (Will also) die — mayyitūna is the plural form 'they (are) mortal', 'they will die', confirming that the disbelievers too are subject to death.

parts.en: (they will) die, they are mortal (masculine plural)

4.grammar: Mayyitūn is the indefinite nominative plural of mayyit (mortal/dead), masculine sound plural form (-ūna). It is the predicate of the inna construction: 'wa-innahum mayyitūn' — 'and indeed they will die'. It parallels the singular mayyitun addressed to the Prophet in the previous clause.
4.root: م-و-ت (m-w-t) — to die; death; mortal

1.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
1.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

2.meaning: 'Indeed you (plural)' — the emphatic particle inna ('truly, indeed, surely'), which strongly affirms and stresses the statement that follows, fused with the attached pronoun 'you (all)'. Inna has no single English word; it functions to underline certainty.
2.grammar: Inna is an emphasising particle that introduces and strengthens a sentence; grammatically it places the following noun or pronoun in the accusative-like role of its 'subject'. The attached -kum is the masculine plural object/possessive pronoun 'you (all)'. Together: 'indeed you (all)…'.

3.meaning: The noun 'day' — a span of time, often used for a momentous Day or appointed time; in the accusative it frequently functions as 'on the day (when…)', marking the time at which something occurs.
3.grammar: A masculine noun bearing the -a (accusative) ending. As an adverb of time this ending typically gives the sense 'on the day…', fixing the moment of an event.
3.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, a period of time

4.meaning: "the Resurrection" — the standing-up of all people from death to be judged; literally the act of rising or standing up.
4.grammar: The al- prefix means "the." The -i ending (on the feminine -t) is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ("the … OF this") or follows a preposition.
4.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise

5.meaning: 'With / in the presence of / near' — an adverb of place and relation meaning at, by, in the sight or estimation of someone. It indicates nearness, possession, or what holds in someone's view (as in 'with Allah' = in His sight).
5.grammar: An adverb of place that is always followed by a noun it relates to. It carries a fixed -a ending; this accusative-type vowel is characteristic of such adverbs of place and shows the word is functioning to locate something ('at, near, in the presence of').

6.meaning: 'Your Lord' — Rabb denotes the Master, Owner, Sustainer, and Nurturer who creates, possesses, and brings each thing to its completion; joined to 'your' (plural).
6.grammar: A noun 'Lord' in the genitive case (the -i ending), which typically follows a preposition or links it to a preceding noun ('… of …'). The suffix -kum is the possessive 'your' addressed to a group.
6.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship: nurturing, mastering, owning, sustaining

7.meaning: Will dispute / will contend — takhtaṣimūna is an imperfect verb meaning 'you (all) will argue with each other', 'you will quarrel', referring to disputes on the Day of Judgment.

parts.en: you will dispute, you will argue with each other (plural)

7.grammar: Form VIII imperfect verb (second masculine plural) from root kh-ṣ-m, meaning to dispute, to quarrel, to litigate. Form VIII ifta'ala adds mutuality. The verse: 'Then, on the Day of Resurrection, before your Lord you will dispute with one another.' Refers to mutual recriminations between leaders and followers, or disbelievers arguing among themselves.
7.root: خ-ص-م (kh-ṣ-m) — to dispute, to litigate, to contend; an adversary

1.meaning: A compound meaning 'then whoever' or 'so whoever'. It combines 'then/so' with the conditional/relative 'who', introducing whatever person meets a stated condition.
1.grammar: The connector fa- ('then/so', often answering or following a condition) joined to man ('whoever / the one who'), which refers to people and introduces a condition: 'whoever does X…'. man does not change its ending; the clause after it supplies the rest of the meaning.

2.meaning: An elative adjective meaning 'more / most wrongdoing, unjust, or oppressive' — comparing degrees of ẓulm (placing things out of their rightful place, transgression).
2.grammar: An elative (comparative/superlative) noun on the pattern afʿal, meaning 'more/most unjust'. It ends in -u (nominative), the case typical of a subject or predicate.
2.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — wrongdoing, injustice, putting something where it does not belong

3.meaning: A compound meaning 'than one who / than whoever' — combining the preposition of comparison 'than' with the relative pronoun 'who', used to compare a person against others.
3.grammar: The preposition 'min' (here 'than', used after elatives) followed by the indeclinable relative 'man' ('who'). The final nūn of 'min' undergoes regressive assimilation into the following mīm of 'man', producing a doubled mīm; the resulting shadda sits on the mīm of 'man'. Both words are indeclinable particles and take no case ending.

4.meaning: Lies / he lies — kadhaba is the perfect verb 'he lied', 'he told falsehood', used to describe those who attribute lies to Allah.
4.grammar: Form I perfect verb (third masculine singular) from root k-dh-b, meaning to lie or tell falsehood. Used in the verse describing the worst wrongdoer — 'Who is more unjust than one who lies against Allah (kadhaba ʿalā Allāh) or who denies the truth when it comes to him?'
4.root: ك-ذ-ب (k-dh-b) — to lie, to tell falsehood

5.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
5.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
5.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

6.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
6.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

7.meaning: And/but he denied, called (something) a lie, treated as false. The doubled middle consonant marks an intensive verb: to vigorously reject something as untrue, to give it the lie.
7.grammar: A past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he ...ed'). The final -a is the standard past-tense ending. The doubled middle letter (form II, shown by the shadda) makes it intensive/transitive: actively rejecting something as false; the transliteration 'kadhdhaba' doubles the 'dh' to reflect this. The prefixed wa- means 'and' or, in contrast, 'but'.
7.root: ك-ذ-ب (k-dh-b) — lying, falsehood

8.meaning: The truth — bil-ṣidqi means 'with the truth' or 'bringing the truth', bi- is the preposition and al-ṣidq is 'the truth/sincerity'.
8.grammar: Bi- is a preposition that here indicates accompaniment or what is brought. Al-ṣidq is a noun from root ṣ-d-q in the definite genitive after bi-. The verse contrasts the one who lies against Allah with the one who comes with the truth (jāʾa bil-ṣidq) — referring to the Prophet and those who believe.
8.root: ص-د-ق (ṣ-d-q) — to be truthful, to confirm as true; truth, sincerity

9.meaning: A particle meaning 'when' or 'at the time that', used to point back to a past moment or event and introduce a recollection of something that occurred.
9.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it has no case ending and never changes form). It signals a point in past time, typically introducing a clause that recalls 'the time when' something happened.

10.meaning: It came to him / he came to him — arrival reaching a particular person. The act of coming or arriving, directed toward someone.
10.grammar: A past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he/it came'), with the final -a marking a completed action; the attached -hu is the object 'him' (the one reached or come to).
10.root: ج-ي-ء (j-y-ʾ) — to come, arrive

11.meaning: "Is it not …? / Is … not …?" A questioning "is not," combining the question-marker "a-" with the negative verb "laysa" ("is not"), used to ask a question that expects the answer "yes, it is."
11.grammar: The negating verb laysa ("is/are not") prefixed with the question-marker a- ("…?"). Such "is it not …?" questions typically invite agreement ("yes, indeed it is"). Laysa is a special verb that negates a statement of being; it carries no tense-ending of the ordinary kind here.

12.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
12.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
12.root: — (particle)

13.meaning: Jahannam — a proper name for the Fire of punishment in the Hereafter, the abode of torment. It is a name rather than a descriptive common noun.
13.grammar: A proper name. Because it is a special, non-fully-inflecting noun (it does not take tanwīn), it shows the -a ending in places where most nouns would otherwise take -i; here the single -a serves for both accusative and genitive positions. As a name it carries no general dictionary 'meaning' but designates the abode of punishment.
13.root: — (a proper name; commonly treated as having no Arabic triliteral root)

14.meaning: An abode / a dwelling place — mathwan is a noun meaning a dwelling, a resting place, or an abode — here referring to Hell as the dwelling of the liars.

parts.en: a dwelling, an abode, a resting place

14.grammar: Mathwā is a Form I noun of place (mafʿal pattern) from root th-w-y, meaning a place of staying or dwelling. In the indefinite accusative (tanwīn fatḥa -an). The verse: 'Is there not in Hell an abode (mathwan) for the arrogant?' — rhetorically affirming the punishment awaiting them.
14.root: ث-و-ي (th-w-y) — to stay, to dwell, to reside; a dwelling place

15.meaning: For/to those who reject faith — the active participle 'kāfir' (one who covers over, conceals, and so denies the truth) in its sound masculine plural, preceded by the preposition 'li-' meaning 'to' or 'for'.
15.grammar: The 'li-' prefix means 'to/for'. The '-īna' ending is the sound masculine plural in its genitive/accusative (oblique) form, used after a preposition; it marks 'the rejecters' as the object of 'for'. The base is an active participle: 'one who is rejecting/covering up faith'.
15.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal, and thus reject or disbelieve

1.meaning: A connector meaning 'and the one who/which', joining a clause and pointing to a single masculine person or thing ('and that which…').
1.grammar: Built from the joining particle wa- ('and/but') plus the masculine singular relative pronoun alladhī ('the one who/which'). A relative pronoun introduces a description and stands for a definite masculine person or thing; its form is fixed and does not change for grammatical case.

2.meaning: He/it came, arrived, or came about — the act of coming into presence or of something occurring.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb with no prefix and no personal suffix, naming a completed act by a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it came'). All three letters here are root letters: jā spells the first radical plus the lengthened weak middle radical, and the final hamza (ء) is the third root consonant — not an ending. The fatḥa (-a) on that hamza is simply the past-tense vocalization for a 'he' subject sitting on the last root letter; there is no separable suffix.

3.meaning: The truth — bil-ṣidqi means 'with the truth' or 'bringing the truth', bi- is the preposition and al-ṣidq is 'the truth/sincerity'.
3.grammar: Bi- is a preposition that here indicates accompaniment or what is brought. Al-ṣidq is a noun from root ṣ-d-q in the definite genitive after bi-. The verse contrasts the one who lies against Allah with the one who comes with the truth (jāʾa bil-ṣidq) — referring to the Prophet and those who believe.
3.root: ص-د-ق (ṣ-d-q) — to be truthful, to confirm as true; truth, sincerity

4.meaning: And believed / and confirmed (as true) — waṣaddaqa means 'and he confirmed the truth', 'and he believed', from ṣaddaqa (to believe, to confirm).

parts.en: he believed, he confirmed (the truth), he accepted as true

4.grammar: Wa- is the conjunction. Ṣaddaqa is Form II perfect (third masculine singular) from root ṣ-d-q, meaning to accept as true, to believe, to confirm. The verse describes the one who brings the truth and the one who confirms it (waṣaddaqa bihi = and believed in it) — these are the people of taqwā.
4.root: ص-د-ق (ṣ-d-q) — to be truthful; to confirm as true, to believe

5.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
5.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

6.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'those' — pointing to people or things that are distant or already known. It singles out a group ('those ones', 'it is those who').
6.grammar: A plural demonstrative pronoun, 'those'. It is fixed in form (no case endings). The -ka element signals distance/remoteness, pointing to something far off or notable. It can refer to people of either gender.

7.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (masculine plural). Standing on its own, it typically adds emphasis or marks the group out as the focus ('they, specifically', 'it is they who').
7.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It takes no case endings; the base is hum, and the final vowel appears as -u (humu) as a connecting vowel to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a definite article. Standing alone, it commonly emphasises or isolates the subject.

8.meaning: Those who have taqwā — the God-conscious, the mindful and dutiful. It describes people who keep a vigilant awareness of Allah, guarding themselves against wrongdoing and shielding themselves from His displeasure out of reverent care.

parts.en: one who is God-conscious / guards himself

8.grammar: The l- prefix is 'the'. This is an active participle (one who does the action). The -ūna ending marks a masculine plural in the subject (nominative) form, i.e. the ones who carry out the guarding/mindfulness.
8.root: و-ق-ي (w-q-y) — to guard, protect, shield oneself

1.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
1.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

2.meaning: A short, highly versatile particle 'mā.' It can mean 'what' or 'that which,' can negate ('not'), and can serve as an intensifier attached to another word. Its precise force depends on what it accompanies, but its core is to point to a thing or to add emphasis.
2.grammar: A multifunctional particle. It does not take case endings. Depending on usage it can be a relative ('that which'), an interrogative ('what?'), a negator ('not'), or — when joined to another particle — an emphasizer. It is uninflected and indeclinable.

3.meaning: They will / they wish — to want, will, or desire something; an act of the will choosing or intending that a thing be.
3.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) verb. The ya- prefix with the -ūna ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they will / they wish'), and -ūna also signals the indicative mood (a plain statement of fact).
3.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʾ) — to will, wish, want; thing

4.meaning: 'With / in the presence of / near' — an adverb of place and relation meaning at, by, in the sight or estimation of someone. It indicates nearness, possession, or what holds in someone's view (as in 'with Allah' = in His sight).
4.grammar: An adverb of place that is always followed by a noun it relates to. It carries a fixed -a ending; this accusative-type vowel is characteristic of such adverbs of place and shows the word is functioning to locate something ('at, near, in the presence of').
4.root: — (adverb of place)

5.meaning: 'Their Lord' — the base 'rabb' means Lord, Master, Sustainer: the one who owns, nurtures, governs, and brings to maturity. As a divine title it conveys Allah as Creator and Sustainer of all.
5.grammar: The noun 'rabb' ('Lord, Sustainer') with the attached pronoun '-him' ('their'). The '-i' before the pronoun is the genitive case, the form used after a preposition or, as in a possessive linkage, to show belonging ('of/their').
5.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, master, sustain; lordship

6.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
6.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

7.meaning: (Is the) reward — jazāu is a noun meaning reward, recompense, or requital, in the nominative as a predicate.
7.grammar: Jazāʾ is a Form I noun from root j-z-y, in the nominative (jazāʾu without tanwīn as it is in a construct state — jazāʾu l-muḥsinīn = the reward of the good-doers). It refers to the complete and perfect recompense that Allah will give to those who did good.
7.root: ج-ز-ي (j-z-y) — to recompense, to requite; reward, requital

8.meaning: 'The doers of good / those who act with excellence and beauty'. It denotes people who do what is good and do it well — acting righteously, generously, and with sincerity, as if conscious of being watched by Allah.

parts.en: good-doers / those who excel in doing good

8.grammar: A definite plural active participle (the 'doer' form of the verb 'to do good'). The prefixed al- means 'the'. The ending -īna marks a sound masculine plural in the object/oblique state — the form used when the noun is a direct object or follows a preposition. It refers to male (or mixed) persons characterized by the action.
8.root: ح-س-ن (ḥ-s-n) — to be good, beautiful; to do well and excellently

1.meaning: That Allah will remove — liyukaffira means 'in order that He may expiate/remove', expressing divine purpose in forgiving the worst of the believers' deeds.

parts.en: in order to, so that (particle of purpose)
He may expiate, He may remove (sins), He may cover over (faults)

1.grammar: Li- introduces a purpose clause with the subjunctive. Yukaffira is Form II imperfect subjunctive (third masculine singular) from root k-f-r, meaning to cover, to expiate, to atone for. The Form II yukaffira implies intensive or complete covering of faults. The verse: 'Allah will reward them with the best of what they did and will expiate from them their evil deeds'.
1.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, to conceal; to expiate (kaffara); to disbelieve

2.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
2.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

3.meaning: From them; away from them; concerning them. The preposition ʿan conveys moving away from, departing from, or 'on behalf of / concerning', combined with the pronoun 'them'.
3.grammar: A preposition joined to the attached pronoun -hum, 'them' (referring to a group, grammatically masculine plural). The preposition ʿan basically signals separation or removal ('away from'), and can also mean 'about/concerning' or 'on behalf of' depending on usage.
3.root: — (a preposition; no triliteral verbal root)

4.meaning: (The) worst — aswaʾa is the elative form 'the worst', 'the most evil', referring to the worst of the believers' deeds that Allah will remove.

parts.en: the worst, the most evil (elative/comparative form)

4.grammar: Aswaʾ is the Form IV elative (afsʿal pattern) from root s-w-ʾ, meaning bad/evil. As an elative it means 'worse' or 'the worst'. In the accusative as the object of yukaffira (He will expiate the worst of their deeds). Context: Allah will forgive even the worst deeds done by the people of taqwā.
4.root: س-و-أ (s-w-ʾ) — to be bad, evil; evil, harm, bad deed

5.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
5.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

6.meaning: They did / they worked — to perform a deed or action, to do work. The base word covers purposeful action and labor.
6.grammar: A completed-action (past-tense) verb. The -ū ending marks 'they' (a group of males) as the doers (the silent alif after it is a spelling convention).
6.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, act, work, perform a deed

7.meaning: And (He will) reward them — wayajziyahum means 'and He will recompense them', describing Allah rewarding the believers beyond just forgiving their sins.

parts.en: He will reward, He will recompense

7.grammar: Wa- is the conjunction. Yajziya is Form I imperfect subjunctive (third masculine singular) from root j-z-y, meaning to recompense or reward. It is in the subjunctive after the coordinated purpose clause (liyukaffira… wayajziya). The suffix -hum is the masculine plural object pronoun.
7.root: ج-ز-ي (j-z-y) — to recompense, to reward, to requite

8.meaning: Their reward, wage, or recompense — the due return given for work or deeds. The base word denotes earned payment or compensation, and the attached pronoun makes it 'their' (a group of males or a mixed group).
8.grammar: A noun in the object form: the -a ending (accusative) typically marks the word as the receiver of an action ('the reward' as the thing given). The suffix -hum means 'their / them' for a plural group.
8.root: أ-ج-ر (ʾ-j-r) — reward, wage, recompense for effort

9.meaning: A phrase meaning 'with/according to the best' — combining the preposition 'with/by/according to' and the comparative-superlative form 'best, finest, most excellent', used to indicate the highest or finest measure of something.
9.grammar: A preposition joined to a superlative noun. The prefix bi- means 'with, by, according to'. The -i ending (genitive) is the case regularly required after a preposition; here it links 'best' to whatever follows it ('the best OF …').
9.root: ح-س-ن (ḥ-s-n) — to be good, beautiful, excellent

10.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
10.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

11.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
11.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
11.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

12.meaning: 'They do / they work, they act' — a present-tense verb of doing and working, covering deeds and actions carried out by a group.
12.grammar: Present/imperfect verb. The ya-…-ūna frame marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (do).' The -ūna ending also marks the indicative mood, the plain statement form, as opposed to command or negated-future forms.
12.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, work, act; deeds

1.meaning: "Is it not …? / Is … not …?" A questioning "is not," combining the question-marker "a-" with the negative verb "laysa" ("is not"), used to ask a question that expects the answer "yes, it is."
1.grammar: The negating verb laysa ("is/are not") prefixed with the question-marker a- ("…?"). Such "is it not …?" questions typically invite agreement ("yes, indeed it is"). Laysa is a special verb that negates a statement of being; it carries no tense-ending of the ordinary kind here.

2.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).

Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

3.meaning: Sufficient — bikāfin means 'sufficient', 'enough'; bi- is the intensifying preposition and kāfin is 'one who suffices'.
3.grammar: Bi- here is the particle bi- al-zāʾida (an additional intensifying particle used in predicate position). Kāfin is Form I active participle from root k-f-y, meaning to suffice, to be enough. In the indefinite genitive (tanwīn kasra -in) after the assertive bi-. The verse: 'Is Allah not sufficient for His servant?' — affirming that Allah is all-sufficient.
3.root: ك-ف-ي (k-f-y) — to suffice, to be enough, to be sufficient

4.meaning: His servant / His slave: a human being owned by and wholly devoted to his Master in worship and obedience. The base word denotes one who serves; the attached pronoun specifies that he belongs to Him (Allah).
4.grammar: A masculine noun with a possessive suffix. The -a ending is the accusative case, marking the word as the direct object of a verb (the one acted upon) or otherwise governed into that case. The suffix -hu means 'his/His,' showing possession by a single male/Divine referent.
4.root: ع-ب-د (ʿ-b-d) — to serve, worship, be a devoted slave

5.meaning: And they threaten you — wayukhawwifūnaka means 'and they frighten you (with their false gods)', trying to instill fear in the Prophet about the idols.

parts.en: they frighten, they threaten, they try to scare

5.grammar: Wa- is the conjunction. Yukhawwifūna is Form II imperfect (third masculine plural) from root kh-w-f, meaning to frighten or terrify. The Form II (faʿʿala) adds a causative sense — 'they cause fear'. The suffix -ka is the second-person masculine singular object pronoun. Context: the disbelievers tried to scare the Prophet with their idols as a threat.
5.root: خ-و-ف (kh-w-f) — to fear; to frighten, to cause fear

6.meaning: A connector meaning 'about/concerning those who' or 'by means of those who'. It joins the preposition 'with/about' to a relative pronoun referring to a known group of male (or mixed) persons, 'those who…'.
6.grammar: The bi- is a preposition ('with', 'about', 'by means of'). 'alladhīna' is the plural relative pronoun 'those who', referring to a group of males or a mixed group; it introduces a clause describing them. Being governed by a preposition, the whole phrase functions in the genitive (the object of 'about/with').

7.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
7.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
7.root: — (preposition)

8.meaning: Other than Him / apart from Him / besides Him. A relational word expressing the idea of being below, short of, or to the exclusion of something or someone.

parts.en: other than, apart from, besides, below

8.grammar: A relational noun/quasi-preposition meaning 'apart from / instead of'. It is followed by a possessive pronoun -hi ('Him'), which puts it in the genitive 'of' relationship; the kasra written under the pronoun reflects this genitive linkage.
8.root: — (no triliteral root; a relational particle/noun)

9.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
9.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.
9.root: — (pronoun/particle; no triliteral root)

10.meaning: He lets/leads astray — he causes someone to lose the right way, leaving them to wander from guidance.
10.grammar: A present-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular ('he …'), in the causative pattern ('to cause to stray'). It stands in the jussive/conditional mood (the doubled lām broken apart and given a helping -i to ease pronunciation), typically meaning 'whomever he lets stray …'.
10.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to stray, go astray, lose the way

So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.
11.root: — (proper divine name)

12.meaning: A two-part expression: 'so/then' joined to a negating word 'not.' The first piece links to what precedes (drawing a result or sequence), and the second negates the statement that follows. Together roughly: 'so… not / and so it did not…'
12.grammar: A connective particle fa- ('so, then,' showing result or sequence) plus the negating particle mā. When mā precedes a past-tense verb, it denies that the action happened ('did not…').

13.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
13.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

14.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
14.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
14.root: — (preposition)

15.meaning: A guide — one who shows the way, leads to the right path, or directs others toward what is correct. The indefinite form conveys 'any guide' or 'a guide (at all)'.
15.grammar: An active participle ('one who guides'). It belongs to the class of nouns ending in a weak letter, so the indefinite tanwīn shows up as -in. This -in marks it as indefinite and signals nominative/genitive case: 'a guide'.
15.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — to guide, lead rightly, direct

1.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
1.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

2.meaning: He guides / is guided — to show the right way; depending on form it can mean 'he guides (someone)' or 'he is rightly guided.'
2.grammar: A present-tense verb in the jussive (apocopate) form: the weak final letter is dropped, leaving the bare -i as the trace of the jussive mood. The ya- prefix marks a single masculine doer ('he'), and the shortened form is the one a verb takes when governed by a jussive operator.
2.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — to guide, show the way

7.meaning: A misleader — muḍillin is an active participle meaning 'one who leads astray', describing Allah's judgment about those who misguide others from His path.

parts.en: one who leads astray, a misleader, one who causes misguidance

7.grammar: Form IV active participle (muḍill) from root ḍ-l-l, in the indefinite genitive (tanwīn kasra -in). The Form IV aḍalla means 'to cause to go astray'. The verse: 'And who guides he whom Allah sends astray? And who misleads he whom Allah guides?' — affirming divine control over guidance and misguidance.
7.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to go astray, to be misguided; to lead astray

10.meaning: 'Mighty / strong / dear' — one who is powerful and unassailable, hard to overcome and highly esteemed. The faʿīl pattern gives an intensive, enduring sense.
10.grammar: A preposition bi- ('with/by') attached to an intensive adjective. The final -in is the indefinite genitive ending, which a noun takes after a preposition; the genitive is the case that typically follows prepositions or links a word to a preceding one.
10.root: ع-ز-ز (ʿ-z-z) — might, strength, being unassailable and honoured

11.meaning: Possessor of / the one having — a relational word meaning 'owner of' or 'endowed with,' used to attach a quality or relationship to the noun it describes.
11.grammar: A relational noun meaning 'owner/possessor of,' which must be followed by another noun ('possessor OF …'). It declines for case: dhū (nominative), dhī (genitive), dhā (accusative). The form dhī (ending -ī) is its genitive, used when it follows a preposition or describes a preceding genitive noun. It never stands alone; it always governs a following noun.
11.root: — (a relational noun meaning 'possessor of'; no verbal root)

12.meaning: Retribution, requital, or just vengeance: the act of exacting due penalty for wrongdoing. It carries the sense of a rightful, measured response to offense rather than arbitrary revenge.
12.grammar: A verbal noun of the eighth verb form (the iftiʿāl pattern), naming the action of exacting requital. The final -in ending combines the genitive case (used after prepositions, after an oath, or to link a word to a preceding noun in an 'of' relationship) with nunation (the -n sound), which marks it as indefinite.
12.root: ن-ق-م (n-q-m) — to avenge, exact penalty, requite

1.meaning: A combination meaning 'and surely if' — introducing a hypothetical condition ('if…') sworn by an implied oath, so that the outcome is strongly anticipated; roughly 'and by all means, if…'.
1.grammar: A cluster of particles, not a noun or verb, so it takes no case ending: wa- 'and', the lam al-qasam (the 'lam of swearing') that marks the following condition as sworn by an implied oath, and in 'if' which sets up the condition. This oath-lam construction correlates with a later response clause that itself carries emphasis (an emphatic lam plus the 'nūn of emphasis' on its verb), giving the sense 'and [I swear] if … they would surely …'.

2.meaning: To ask, question, or request — to put a query to someone or seek something from them. With the endings attached it means 'you asked them,' a completed act of questioning directed at a group.
2.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb describing a completed action. The suffix -ta marks the doer as second-person masculine singular ('you'); the further suffix -hum is the direct object 'them.'

3.meaning: A versatile word meaning 'who / whoever / the one who.' It can ask a question ('who?') or introduce a clause ('whoever does…'), referring to persons.
3.grammar: An indeclinable particle/pronoun with a fixed form (it does not change for case). Used for rational beings ('who'), functioning either as an interrogative ('who?') or as a conditional/relative ('whoever, the one who').

4.meaning: 'He created' — to bring into being, to originate and shape something that did not exist before, from the root denoting creation and the fashioning of things from nothing.
4.grammar: Past tense, third-person masculine singular ('he'), completed action ('he created'). This is a form I verb of the CaCaCa pattern. The masculine singular 'he' here is the unmarked (zero-suffix) form — there is no separate person ending; the final -a is the inherent stem vowel of the base pattern, not a person or tense suffix.
4.root: خ-ل-ق (kh-l-q) — creating, originating, shaping

5.meaning: The heavens / the skies — the plural of 'heaven', referring to the skies above and the celestial realms; the elevated expanse over the earth.
5.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun with the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the heavens') or follows a preposition. In the sound feminine plural, this -i form also covers what would be an object role.

6.meaning: 'and the earth' — the ground, land, or the planet earth; the world we stand upon, often paired with the heavens to mean all of creation.
6.grammar: A feminine noun, prefixed with 'and' and 'the.' The -a ending is accusative, the case typically marking the object of a verb (the thing acted upon) or a noun governed by certain particles.

7.meaning: An emphatic assertion 'they will surely say / they will certainly say.' The word fuses an oath-like emphasis with a future statement of speaking, leaving no doubt that the utterance will occur. The heavy doubled ending drives home the certainty.
7.grammar: A present/future verb made doubly emphatic. The opening la- means 'surely'; the ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine subject; and the heavy -nna suffix (the 'energetic' ending) intensifies it to 'they will most certainly say.' Together la-…-nna is a fixed pattern of strong affirmation about something yet to happen.
7.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, speak, utter

8.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
8.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.
8.root: — (proper divine name)

9.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
9.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.
9.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, speak

10.meaning: A composite expression meaning roughly 'have you then considered / tell me' — it joins a questioning particle, a connective, and the verb 'you saw', used to invite reflection on what follows.
10.grammar: A past-tense verb 'you saw/considered' fronted by two particles: a- (the interrogative, turning it into a question) and fa- ('then/so'). The suffix -tum is the subject ending for 'you all' (masculine plural) on a completed-action verb — the tā belongs to this suffix, not the stem; idiomatically the whole asks 'have you considered?'.
10.root: ر-ء-ي (r-ʾ-y) — to see, perceive, consider

11.meaning: A short, highly versatile particle 'mā.' It can mean 'what' or 'that which,' can negate ('not'), and can serve as an intensifier attached to another word. Its precise force depends on what it accompanies, but its core is to point to a thing or to add emphasis.
11.grammar: A multifunctional particle. It does not take case endings. Depending on usage it can be a relative ('that which'), an interrogative ('what?'), a negator ('not'), or — when joined to another particle — an emphasizer. It is uninflected and indeclinable.
11.root: — (particle; no root)

12.meaning: A verb meaning 'you (all) call upon, invoke, summon, or pray to.' The root spans calling out, naming, inviting, and supplicating — especially calling on someone for help.
12.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ta- prefix with the -ūna ending marks 'you all' (masculine plural) as the doers. The final -na is the indicative marker, signalling an ongoing or habitual action (a complete, non-shortened present-tense verb).
12.root: د-ع-و (d-ʿ-w) — to call, invoke, summon, pray

13.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
13.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
13.root: — (preposition)

14.meaning: A noun used to mean 'besides', 'other than', 'apart from', or 'short of'. It points to something or someone set apart from, or lower/lesser than, a named party. Often used in the phrase 'besides Allah'.
14.grammar: 'dūn' functions as an adverb-like noun of place/relation. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, which appears because it follows a preposition (such as 'min', 'from') and because it links to a following noun ('other than …'). It commonly heads the construction 'besides/other than [someone]'.
14.root: د-و-ن (d-w-n) — to be low/beneath, to fall short; hence 'below, other than, besides'

15.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
15.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

16.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
16.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

17.meaning: Allah intended for me — arādaniya means 'He intended for me', 'He willed (something) to me', where arāda is 'He intended' and -niya is 'me'.

parts.en: He intended, He willed, He wanted
me (first person singular object suffix, with pause form yāʾ)

17.grammar: Arāda is Form IV perfect (third masculine singular) from root r-w-d/r-y-d, meaning to intend, to will, to want. The suffix -niya is the first-person singular object pronoun with the full yāʾ. Context: 'Say: If Allah had intended to harm me, could these that you call upon besides Allah remove His harm?' — demonstrating Allah's complete sovereignty.
17.root: ر-و-د/ر-ي-د (r-w-d) — to intend, to will, to want; to seek

18.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
18.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

19.meaning: 'With harm', 'with affliction / hurt'. The phrase joins the preposition 'with / by means of' to a word for harm, injury, or distress. The word is in its indefinite form: 'some harm', 'any affliction'.
19.grammar: A preposition 'with' attached to the noun 'harm'. The -in ending is the indefinite genitive: the genitive case (required after a preposition) combined with the 'an/some' nunation that marks the noun as unspecified — 'with some harm'.

20.meaning: An interrogative particle that turns a statement into a yes/no question, roughly "is it that…?" or "do…?". It can also carry a rhetorical or expectant tone rather than a literal request for information.
20.grammar: A question particle placed before a sentence to ask whether something is the case. It has no case ending and does not change form; it simply marks the words that follow as a yes/no question.

21.meaning: 'They / them' — the detached subject pronoun for a group of females, standing on its own to mean 'they (feminine)' or to emphasize the female group as the topic.
21.grammar: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' for a group of females. Because it is a separate word, it normally serves as the subject of a sentence or gives emphasis ('they themselves'). Its form is fixed and does not take case endings.

22.meaning: Removers — kāshifātu is a feminine plural active participle meaning 'those who remove', 'those who uncover', referring to whether the idols can remove Allah's intended harm.

parts.en: removers, those who uncover/lift (harm); feminine plural

22.grammar: Form I active participle (kāshifa), feminine plural (kāshifāt) from root k-sh-f, meaning to uncover, to remove, to expose. In the construct state (iḍāfa) with the following genitive. Context: 'Could these remove (kāshifātu) the harm He intended?' — a rhetorical question showing that only Allah can lift harm, not idols.
22.root: ك-ش-ف (k-sh-f) — to uncover, to remove, to expose, to reveal

23.meaning: (Of) harm (from) Him — ḍurrihi means 'His harm' or 'the harm from Him', with ḍurr (harm) and -hi (His/from Him).

parts.en: His (from Him — third person masculine singular possessive)

23.grammar: Ḍurr is a noun from root ḍ-r-r in the genitive (iḍāfa with the possessive). The suffix -hi is third-person masculine singular. Together: 'the harm He (Allah) intended' — in the context of asking whether the idols could remove the harm that Allah might will.

24.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
24.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

25.meaning: If He intended for me — arādanī here means 'if He intended for me (mercy)', parallel to the previous verse about Allah intending harm, now asking about Allah's mercy.
25.grammar: Arāda is Form IV perfect (third masculine singular) from root r-w-d. The suffix -nī (shorter form, in pause) is first-person singular object. This is the second half of the rhetorical question: 'If He intended mercy for me, could they withhold His mercy?' — demonstrating absolute divine sovereignty.
25.root: ر-و-د (r-w-d) — to intend, to will, to want

26.meaning: With mercy / by mercy: tender compassion and active kindness that relieves and benefits. The noun names mercy as a quality and an outpouring of grace.
26.grammar: A feminine noun governed by the preposition bi- ('with/by'). The -in ending is the genitive case with nunation — genitive because it follows a preposition, and the final -n marks it as indefinite ('a mercy').

27.meaning: An interrogative particle that turns a statement into a yes/no question, roughly "is it that…?" or "do…?". It can also carry a rhetorical or expectant tone rather than a literal request for information.
27.grammar: A question particle placed before a sentence to ask whether something is the case. It has no case ending and does not change form; it simply marks the words that follow as a yes/no question.

28.meaning: 'They / them' — the detached subject pronoun for a group of females, standing on its own to mean 'they (feminine)' or to emphasize the female group as the topic.
28.grammar: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' for a group of females. Because it is a separate word, it normally serves as the subject of a sentence or gives emphasis ('they themselves'). Its form is fixed and does not take case endings.

29.meaning: Withholders — mumsikātu is a feminine plural active participle meaning 'those who hold back', 'those who withhold', referring to the idols hypothetically withholding Allah's mercy.

parts.en: withholders, those who hold back/restrain; feminine plural active participle

29.grammar: Form IV active participle (mumsika), feminine plural (mumsikāt) from root m-s-k, meaning to hold, to retain, to withhold. In the construct state (iḍāfa) with the following genitive. The rhetorical question: 'Or could they withhold (mumsikātu) His mercy?' — answer: no, only Allah controls mercy.
29.root: م-س-ك (m-s-k) — to hold, to grasp, to retain, to withhold

30.meaning: His mercy — His compassion, tenderness, and loving-kindness that actively bestows good and relief. "Raḥmah" is mercy as an outpouring of care, here possessed by Him.
30.grammar: A feminine singular noun with an attached possessive "His." The -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun or preposition ("… of …"). The pronoun appears as -hi (rather than -hu) because it follows that -i vowel.

31.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
31.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

32.meaning: Enough for me, sufficient for me — that which suffices, fully meets one's need, and makes anything further unnecessary. The attached pronoun directs that sufficiency to the speaker ('for me').
32.grammar: A noun meaning 'sufficiency' with the attached pronoun -iya ('me/my'). Such a noun plus the 'me' pronoun forms a statement of the type 'X is enough for me.' The linking -i- before the pronoun reflects the possessive/attached-pronoun connection.
32.root: ح-س-ب (ḥ-s-b) — to reckon, count, suffice, be enough

33.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
33.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

34.meaning: A preposition fused with a pronoun, meaning 'upon him', 'on him', or 'toward him'. It marks the one to whom an action is directed or upon whom something rests.
34.grammar: The preposition 'upon/on' with an attached object pronoun -hi ('him', third-person masculine singular); its -i vowel is the regular form the pronoun takes after the 'y' sound. Paired with a verb of turning, this 'upon/toward him' marks the person the action reaches.

35.meaning: (He) puts trust — yatawakkalu is an imperfect verb meaning 'he relies on', 'he puts his trust (in Allah)', describing the state of one who is truly trusting in Allah.

parts.en: he puts his trust (in Allah), he relies (on Allah)

35.grammar: Form V imperfect verb (third masculine singular) from root w-k-l, meaning to rely, to entrust, to put one's trust in. Form V (tafaʿʿala) adds an intensive reflexive sense — fully committing oneself to relying on another. The verse: 'Whoever puts his trust in Allah, He is sufficient for him (ḥasbuhu).'
35.root: و-ك-ل (w-k-l) — to entrust, to rely on; a representative, an agent

36.meaning: Those who place their trust and reliance — people who depend wholly on another (especially on Allah), committing their affairs to Him.

parts.en: one who trusts/relies (active participle, Form V)

36.grammar: The definite article al- ('the') plus the active participle of Form V (tawakkala, 'to put one's trust'). The -ūna ending marks a sound masculine plural in the nominative case — the case typically used for the subject of a sentence ('the ones who trust').
36.root: و-ك-ل (w-k-l) — to entrust, to rely upon

1.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
1.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

2.meaning: 'O my people!' — a vocative call: 'people' (one's own community/folk) addressed directly, with 'my' attached. A speaker uses it to summon and appeal to his own community.
2.grammar: The particle yā- is the vocative ('O …'), used to call or address someone. The final -i here is the remnant of the possessive 'my' (the fuller -ī), commonly shortened to -i in direct address, so the whole means 'O my people!' The case ending proper is suppressed because the noun is being called, not used as subject or object.
2.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, to rise; a people who stand together

3.meaning: A command addressed to a group: 'Do!', 'Act!', 'Work!' — an imperative urging people to carry out deeds or labor.
3.grammar: An imperative (command) verb addressed to a plural 'you'. The '-ū' ending is the plural-subject marker, so it commands more than one person: 'all of you, do/act'. The initial alif is a helping vowel to begin the word.
3.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, to work, to act; deeds

4.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
4.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

5.meaning: A noun meaning one's station, standing, rank, or status — the position or capacity a person occupies, whether literal place or figurative standing. With the attached 'your', it means 'your station' or 'your standing/way'.
5.grammar: A feminine noun ('station/standing/rank') in a possessive (iḍāfa) construction. Its tāʾ marbūṭa, normally pronounced '-a', surfaces as '-at-' when the word is in construct and carries a following possessor; the case vowel '-i' on it here is genitive (typical after a preposition or as a possessed noun). The suffix '-kum' is the attached possessive pronoun 'your' for a group.
5.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist; standing, station, status

6.meaning: 'Truly I' or 'indeed I' — the emphatic affirming particle inna ('truly, indeed, certainly'), which strengthens and confirms a statement, joined to the pronoun 'I'.
6.grammar: An emphasizing particle with an attached pronoun. 'Inna' is a particle of emphasis and affirmation that introduces a statement and lends it certainty ('it is certainly the case that…'). The attached -ī is the first-person singular pronoun ('I / me') in the object form this particle requires. Together: 'Indeed I…'.

7.meaning: Active participle meaning 'one who does/works', i.e. a doer, worker, or one engaged in action. Stated indefinitely, it means 'a worker' or 'one who acts'.
7.grammar: An active participle (the 'doer' of the verb 'to work/do') used as a noun. The '-un' ending (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite and in the nominative state — typically the role of a subject or the thing being described.
7.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, to work, to act; deeds

8.meaning: A two-part marker meaning 'then/so' plus 'shall/will.' It announces something forthcoming as a consequence: the particle sawfa points to the future, generally a more remote or emphatic future than the shorter prefix sa-.
8.grammar: A linking particle fa- ('then/so,' signalling result or sequence) joined to the future particle sawfa, which is placed before a present-tense verb to throw its action into the future ('will/shall …').

9.meaning: A verb addressed to a group: 'you (all) know', 'you have knowledge', 'you are aware'. From the root meaning 'to know'.
9.grammar: The 'ta-' prefix marks a present/future verb addressed to 'you'. The '-ūna' ending marks a masculine plural subject and is the full 'indicative' form, signalling an ongoing, factual statement ('you (all) do know'), as opposed to the shortened '-ū' used after certain particles.
9.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — to know, knowledge

1.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
1.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

2.meaning: 'It comes to him / will come to him' — the act of arriving at or reaching a person, with an attached 'him' as the one reached.
2.grammar: A present-tense verb with the ya- prefix marking a third-person masculine singular subject ('it/he comes'). The attached -hi is the object 'him' (the -i vowel of this pronoun appears after an -i sound). The form is read as a sound (indicative/subjunctive) present rather than a command.
2.root: أ-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come, arrive, bring; to reach or befall.

3.meaning: Painful punishment, torment, or chastisement — suffering imposed as a penalty.
3.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The ending -un (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a punishment') and in the nominative case, typically used for the subject or for the thing said to exist.
3.root: ع-ذ-ب (ʿ-dh-b) — to punish, torment, chastise

4.meaning: 'It disgraces him / will disgrace him' — to bring shame, humiliation, and abasement upon someone; an attached 'him' is the one disgraced.
4.grammar: A present-tense verb of Form IV (the causative type — to 'bring' the state about). The yu- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('it/he'). The attached -hi is the object 'him'. The weak final root letter shows as the long -ī before the pronoun.
4.root: خ-ز-ي (kh-z-y) — disgrace, humiliation, shame, ignominy.

5.meaning: 'And it descends / alights' — to come down upon, settle on, or befall; ḥalla also carries the sense of becoming due or lawful, but here the core is 'to land upon'.
5.grammar: The wa- prefix means 'and'. The ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('it/he'). The final -u is the indicative ending, signalling a plain present-tense statement with no governing particle.
5.root: ح-ل-ل (ḥ-l-l) — to alight, settle, untie; hence what 'comes down,' and also what is loosed and so permitted.

6.meaning: A preposition fused with a pronoun, meaning 'upon him', 'on him', or 'toward him'. It marks the one to whom an action is directed or upon whom something rests.
6.grammar: The preposition 'upon/on' with an attached object pronoun -hi ('him', third-person masculine singular); its -i vowel is the regular form the pronoun takes after the 'y' sound. Paired with a verb of turning, this 'upon/toward him' marks the person the action reaches.

7.meaning: Painful punishment, torment, or chastisement — suffering imposed as a penalty.
7.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The ending -un (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a punishment') and in the nominative case, typically used for the subject or for the thing said to exist.
7.root: ع-ذ-ب (ʿ-dh-b) — to punish, torment, chastise

8.meaning: "lasting, enduring, permanent, abiding" — an active participle describing something that stays in place, persists, or is established and ongoing.
8.grammar: An active participle (form IV) functioning as an adjective/noun ("one that stays, abiding"). The "mu-" prefix marks the doer/agent of the action. The final "-un" (tanwīn ḍamma) is the indefinite nominative ending, marking the word as indefinite ("a lasting one") and as a subject or predicate rather than an object.
8.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise, remain, establish

1.meaning: A two-part expression: an emphatic particle that strongly affirms and confirms a statement ('truly, indeed, certainly'), fused with the attached pronoun 'we.' Together: 'truly we…' / 'indeed we…'
1.grammar: The particle inna gives strong emphasis and certainty to the clause it opens. The attached -ā is the pronoun 'we,' serving as the subject being emphasized: 'truly we…'

2.meaning: We sent down — to cause something to descend or be revealed from a higher source to a lower; classically used of revelation sent down from on high.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb of the causative (fourth) form, meaning to make something come down. The attached -nā is the subject pronoun 'we', marking the action as completed and done by a 'we' (a form of majestic/collective speech when used of Allah).
2.root: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — to descend, come down, be sent down

3.meaning: "upon you / to you / against you" — the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over') with the 'you' pronoun, carrying senses of resting upon, being directed to, or bearing upon someone.
3.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The base ʿalā shifts to ʿalay- when a pronoun is added. The suffix -ka means 'you' (second-person masculine singular). Prepositions themselves take no case ending.

4.meaning: The Book, the Scripture — a written revelation; the term for a divinely revealed text.
4.grammar: A definite noun ('the Book') with attached 'al-' ('the'). The final '-a' ending is the accusative case, typically marking the word as the direct object of a verb.
4.root: ك-ت-ب (k-t-b) — to write; a writing, book

5.meaning: To the people, for mankind — addressed or directed toward human beings in general; 'an-nās' is the collective word for 'people, humankind'.
5.grammar: The preposition 'li-' (to/for) joined to 'an-nās' (the people); the article's 'a' drops in pronunciation and its 'l' assimilates into the noun's 'n' (shown by the doubling). The -i ending is the genitive case, required because the word follows the preposition 'li-'. 'nās' is a collective noun for humankind with no singular of its own root form.

6.meaning: 'With the truth / by means of what is true and right.' Combines the preposition 'with/by' and 'the truth' — that which is real, established, correct, and rightfully due, as opposed to falsehood.
6.grammar: A noun governed by the attached preposition bi- ('with/by'). The -i ending is the genitive case, which is required after a preposition; here it links 'the truth' to 'with', giving 'with the truth'.
6.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, right, reality, that which is established and due

7.meaning: A two-part connector meaning 'so/then whoever'. It joins a clause to what precedes ('so', 'then') and introduces a conditional or general statement about any person who does something ('whoever, anyone who').
7.grammar: The prefix fa- is a connecting particle meaning 'so/then', linking this to a prior statement. man is a conditional/relative word for persons ('whoever'); its base form is man, and the final vowel here is read -i simply to ease pronunciation before a following consonant cluster, not a case ending.

8.meaning: He became guided / found the right way / accepted guidance — the verb (Form VIII) means to take the right path, follow guidance, and be rightly directed; it implies responding to and embracing guidance.

parts.en: became guided / followed the right way

8.grammar: A past-tense (completed-action) verb in the Form VIII pattern (which often carries a reflexive sense — accepting guidance for oneself), with a third-person-masculine-singular subject ('he'). Its weak final root letter appears as a long -ā ending, the usual past-tense shape for such roots.
8.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — to guide, lead aright, show the way

9.meaning: 'Then it is for his own self/soul' — introducing a consequence that the benefit accrues to a person's own self. The nafs is the inner self, soul, or person — the seat of one's individual being.
9.grammar: fa means 'then/so' (a connective showing result). li- is the preposition 'for/to (the benefit of)', which puts the following noun in the genitive. The -i ending is genitive (required after li-). The suffix -hi is the attached possessive pronoun 'his'.
9.root: ن-ف-س (n-f-s) — soul, self, breath, person

10.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
10.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.
10.root: — (pronoun/particle; no triliteral root)

11.meaning: He strayed, lost the way, or went off course — to wander from the right path, whether literally or figuratively (to err, be misguided, or deviate from truth and guidance).
11.grammar: A past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular: 'he went astray'. The bare past-tense form with the -a ending signals a single male (or thing) as the doer of a completed action.
11.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to go astray, lose the way, err

12.meaning: A compound particle 'so it is only …' or 'then indeed only.' It joins a consequence ('so/then') to an emphatic restriction ('only / nothing more than'), confining the statement to exactly what follows.
12.grammar: A cluster of particles: 'fa-' introduces a result ('so/then'), 'inna' gives emphasis ('truly'), and the attached 'mā' turns the emphasis into restriction, so the whole means 'so it is only/nothing but.' These are connective and emphatic words; they have no case ending of their own.

13.meaning: He goes astray / strays / errs / is lost — to wander from the right path, lose one's way, or fall into error. The doubled final consonant belongs to the root.
13.grammar: A present/future-tense verb with the ya- prefix marking a third-person-masculine-singular subject ('he'). The two identical final root letters are merged (a doubled consonant), and the -u vowel on it marks the indicative mood, a plain statement ('he strays').
13.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to go astray, lose the way, err

14.meaning: 'On it / upon it / over it' — the preposition 'alā ('on, upon, against') joined to the pronoun 'it/her', referring to a single feminine or grammatically feminine thing.
14.grammar: 'ʿalā' is a preposition meaning 'on/upon/over'; its ending shifts to -ay when a pronoun is attached. The suffix -hā is the object pronoun for a single feminine (or feminine-gender) thing. Together they mean 'on it'. Words after a preposition stand in the genitive, though attached pronouns like -hā do not visibly change form.

15.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
15.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.
15.root: — (relative pronoun / particle)

16.meaning: 'You' — the standalone, independent pronoun for addressing a single male person directly.
16.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, second-person masculine singular. Unlike attached pronoun suffixes, it stands alone and is typically used to identify or emphasize the subject ('you [yourself]').

17.meaning: A compound meaning 'upon them' or 'against them': the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over, against') joined to the plural pronoun 'them'. It conveys something resting on, being incumbent upon, or weighing against a group.
17.grammar: ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay- before a pronoun. The suffix -him is the attached pronominal suffix for a masculine plural group ('them'); after a preposition it carries genitive/prepositional force, and the -i- vowel reflects its position after this preposition. Together they signal a relationship of something being over, upon, or burdensome to that group.
17.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

18.meaning: A manager / a guardian — biwakīlin means 'with a guardian' or 'as a guardian'; wakīl is one who manages affairs, a trustee or agent.
