8.grammar: A definite noun ('the earth'). The '-a' ending marks the accusative (the 'object' case) — the role of the thing acted upon, e.g. the direct object of a verb. The prefixed 'al-' makes it definite, 'the earth.'
8.root: أ-ر-ض (ʼ-r-ḍ) — earth, land, ground

9.meaning: We may settle — natabawwaʾu means 'we settle ourselves', 'we dwell', 'we take up our abode', describing the freedom the believers will have in Paradise.

parts.en: we settle, we take up abode, we dwell wherever we will

9.grammar: Form V imperfect verb (first plural) from root b-w-ʾ, meaning to settle, to take up residence, to return to one's home. Form V tabawwaʾa adds a reflexive sense — 'we make our dwelling place'. Context: 'We settle in Paradise wherever we will (natabawwaʾu min al-jannati ḥaythu nashāʾu)' — the believers' declaration of their freedom and delight in Paradise.
9.root: ب-و-أ (b-w-ʾ) — to settle, to dwell, to take up abode; a dwelling place

10.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
10.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

11.meaning: The Garden / Paradise — a definite noun literally meaning 'the garden'; the term for the Garden of Paradise, the abode of reward in the Hereafter.
11.grammar: Definite noun: 'al-' is 'the'. The '-i' ending (on the feminine '-at-') is genitive, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF …') or follows a preposition. 'janna' originally means a lush, shaded garden.
11.root: ج-ن-ن (j-n-n) — to cover, conceal (a garden's dense foliage 'covers' the ground)

12.meaning: Wherever / in whatever place — an adverb pointing to an unspecified location, 'in the place where ...'.
12.grammar: An invariable adverb of place ('where / wherever'). Although it ends in -u, it is fixed in form and does not change for case; it is normally followed by a clause stating the situation tied to that place.

13.meaning: We will, We so choose, We please — to will and desire a thing, exercising one's wish and choice. 'Shāʾa' denotes the act of willing that brings a matter about.
13.grammar: A present-tense verb. The na- prefix marks the subject as 'we', and the final -u ending marks the plain, ongoing/habitual present ('we will', as a stated possibility or fact).
13.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʾ) — willing, wishing, choosing; the exercise of will

14.meaning: How excellent! / What a fine thing is …! A fixed expression of praise meaning that the thing named is excellent and goodly — declaring something to be best or most fitting.
14.grammar: The prefix 'fa-' means 'so / and then', linking to what precedes. 'Niʿma' is a frozen verb of praise — it does not conjugate for tense in the ordinary way and is used to extol whatever noun follows as excellent ('how good is …!'). Its counterpart for blame is 'biʾsa' ('how evil is …!').
14.root: ن-ع-م (n-ʿ-m) — goodness, favour, that which is excellent and pleasing

15.meaning: Reward, recompense, wage — the return or compensation given for what one has done; payment for work or deeds.
15.grammar: A noun. The final '-u' is the nominative case ending, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or, as here without nunation, a noun that is the first term of a possessive phrase ('the reward of …'). It denotes a deserved recompense, whether worldly or in the Hereafter.
15.root: أ-ج-ر (ʾ-j-r) — to recompense, reward; wages, reward

16.meaning: The doers / the workers — those who act and put things into practice, especially the ones who do righteous deeds. The word names people defined by their working and acting.
16.grammar: An active participle in the sound masculine plural, made definite by 'al-'. The '-īna' ending is the oblique (genitive/accusative) plural, meaning 'the ones who…'; here it typically follows a possessive link ('the reward of the workers'). It denotes habitual doers — those characterized by working and acting.
16.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, work, act; deed, work

1.meaning: "and you see / would see" — to perceive with the eyes or to behold; also "to regard" something as being a certain way.
1.grammar: A present-tense verb in the second-person masculine singular: the ta- prefix means "you (one man)." This verb comes from a weak root, so its final weak letter shows as the long -ā vowel; in the indicative it expresses ongoing or potential seeing.

2.meaning: The angels — Allah's created beings of light who serve Him perfectly, never disobeying His commands, and carry out His will (including conveying revelation). A collective plural noun referring to them as a group.

parts.en: feminine plural ending (tā marbūṭa) + accusative vowel

2.grammar: A plural noun with the al- prefix ('the'). The word ends in tā marbūṭa (ة), here marking the feminine plural pattern, which itself carries the case vowel; bearing the accusative -a it is pronounced -ta. The accusative typically marks the word as the object of a verb or otherwise governed in that case.
2.root: م-ل-ك (m-l-k) — to possess, have power; 'malak' = angel (alternatively analyzed as أ-ل-ك, ʾ-l-k, 'to send a message')

3.meaning: Surrounding — ḥāffīna is an active participle meaning 'surrounding', 'encircling', describing the angels surrounding the Throne of Allah on the Day of Judgment.

parts.en: surrounding, encircling, gathered around (plural active participle, accusative)

3.grammar: Ḥāffīn is the Form I active participle (ḥāff) in the indefinite accusative plural (-īna) from root ḥ-f-f, meaning to surround, to encircle, to crowd around. As a ḥāl (circumstantial complement) describing the state of the angels: 'And you will see the angels surrounding (ḥāffīna) the Throne from all sides, glorifying their Lord with praise.'
3.root: ح-ف-ف (ḥ-f-f) — to surround, to encircle, to cluster around

4.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
4.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
4.root: — (preposition)

5.meaning: Around — ḥawli means 'around', 'surrounding', 'encircling', indicating the angels' positions surrounding the Throne of Allah.
5.grammar: Ḥawl is a noun from root ḥ-w-l used adverbially/prepositionally to mean 'around', 'about', 'surrounding'. In the genitive after min (from): min ḥawli al-ʿarsh = 'from around the Throne'. Context: 'You will see the angels surrounding the Throne from all around (min ḥawlihi), glorifying with praise of their Lord' — the final grand scene of Surah Az-Zumar.
5.root: ح-و-ل (ḥ-w-l) — around, about; to circle around; power, year

6.meaning: The Throne — the mighty seat of sovereignty and dominion. Literally a throne or canopy of a king; used as an image of supreme authority and rule.
6.grammar: A definite noun in the genitive case (the -i ending). The genitive appears when a noun follows a preposition or is linked to a preceding noun in a possessive 'X of Y' relationship. The l- prefix makes it definite ('the').
6.root: ع-ر-ش (ʿ-r-sh) — throne, canopy, seat of dominion

7.meaning: They declare Allah free of all imperfection and glorify Him — proclaiming His utter purity and transcendence above any flaw, partner, or unworthy attribute. The stem combines praise with the act of removing every defect from the One praised.
7.grammar: A present/ongoing verb on an intensive (doubled-middle) pattern that conveys earnest, repeated action. The yu- prefix with -ūna marks a masculine plural subject doing this continually: 'they glorify'. The final -na shows the full (indicative) form of a real, ongoing action.
7.root: س-ب-ح (s-b-ḥ) — to declare free of imperfection, glorify; to swim/glide swiftly

8.meaning: A phrase meaning 'with the praise of' — joining the preposition 'with/by' to the noun 'praise.' Ḥamd is praise mingled with gratitude and admiration directed to one who deserves it.
8.grammar: A preposition 'bi-' ('with/by') attached to the noun 'praise.' The '-i' ending is genitive, which here follows the preposition and also links 'praise' to a following word ('praise OF …').
8.root: ح-م-د (ḥ-m-d) — to praise (with gratitude and admiration)

9.meaning: 'Their Lord' — the base 'rabb' means Lord, Master, Sustainer: the one who owns, nurtures, governs, and brings to maturity. As a divine title it conveys Allah as Creator and Sustainer of all.
9.grammar: The noun 'rabb' ('Lord, Sustainer') with the attached pronoun '-him' ('their'). The '-i' before the pronoun is the genitive case, the form used after a preposition or, as in a possessive linkage, to show belonging ('of/their').
9.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, master, sustain; lordship

10.meaning: And it was settled/decided/carried out; the bringing of a matter to a final, completed conclusion. Opens with "and" linking it to what precedes.
10.grammar: A past-tense verb in the passive voice, so the action is done to the subject rather than by it ("was decreed/settled"). The vowel pattern with -i- in the stem marks the passive. The final -a/-ya ending marks a third-person masculine singular subject ("it/he"). Prefixed wa- means "and."
10.root: ق-ض-ي (q-ḍ-y) — to decree, decide, conclude, carry out

11.meaning: An adverb of place meaning 'between' or 'among', here joined to the attached pronoun 'them'; together it conveys 'between them / amongst them', signalling something situated in the midst of a group or shared among parties.
11.grammar: An adverb of place (ẓarf) ending in -a, the accusative marker typical of such adverbs, indicating a location or relationship. The attached suffix '-hum' is a possessive/object pronoun meaning 'them' (a group of males or a mixed group).
11.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction, what lies in the midst

12.meaning: 'With the truth / by means of what is true and right.' Combines the preposition 'with/by' and 'the truth' — that which is real, established, correct, and rightfully due, as opposed to falsehood.
12.grammar: A noun governed by the attached preposition bi- ('with/by'). The -i ending is the genitive case, which is required after a preposition; here it links 'the truth' to 'with', giving 'with the truth'.
12.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, right, reality, that which is established and due

13.meaning: And it was said — a statement was uttered or a command was given (by an unnamed speaker).
13.grammar: A past-tense passive verb. The internal vowel pattern (qīla, with 'ī') marks it as passive — the doer is unspecified, so it means 'it was said' rather than 'he said.' The final '-a' is the standard ending of a third-person masculine singular past verb.
13.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, speak, utter

14.meaning: The praise — all commendation, thanks, and laudation. With the article it conveys praise as a whole, in its entirety, belonging by right to the one praised.
14.grammar: A verbal noun with the definite article 'al-'. The '-u' ending is nominative, marking it as the subject/topic of a sentence; with the article it carries the sense of 'all praise' as an entire, comprehensive category.
14.root: ح-م-د (ḥ-m-d) — to praise/commend

15.meaning: A two-part word: the preposition 'li-' meaning 'to', 'for', or 'belonging to', attached to the name 'Allah'. It conveys 'to Allah' or 'for Allah'.
15.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('to/for') pulls the following noun into the genitive case, which is why 'Allah' ends in '-i' (llāhi). The '-i' ending is the regular result of a noun governed by a preposition.

16.meaning: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'my': the One who owns, sustains, nurtures, and governs — combining mastery, ownership, and loving cultivation. With the attached 'my' it is an intimate address, 'my Lord.'
16.grammar: A noun, rabb, with the first-person possessive (the original 'my' yāʾ being reduced to a final -i, so 'my Lord'). The word denotes the Master who creates, owns, and lovingly sustains. Used as a heartfelt vocative, calling upon one's Lord.
16.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

17.meaning: 'The worlds / all created beings' — the entirety of created realms and their inhabitants (humans, jinn, and everything else); a plural conveying 'all that exists'.
17.grammar: A definite masculine sound plural. The '-īna' ending marks the plural in the object/genitive state (used as a non-subject, after a preposition, or after certain particles), as opposed to the subject form '-ūna'.
17.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — to know; (ʿālam) a world, a domain of knowing/created order
